title.zh: 卷三百十五 列傳第七十四 韓億 韓絳 韓維 韓縝
title.en: Volume 315 Biographies 74: Han Yi, Han Jiang, Han Wei, Han Zhen
title.raw: 卷三百十五 列傳第七十四 韓億 韓絳 韓維 韓縝 Volume 315 Biographies 74: Han Yi, Han Jiang, Han Wei, Han Zhen

sentences.zh: 韓億，字宗魏，其先真定靈壽人，徙開封之雍丘。

translations.literal: Han Yi, courtesy name Zongwei, his ancestors were from Lingshou in Zhending and moved to Yongqiu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yi, whose courtesy name was Zongwei, came from a family originally of Lingshou in Zhending that had relocated to Yongqiu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為大理評事、知永城縣，有治聲。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as a reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, and governed Yongcheng County, gaining a reputation for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his jinshi degree, he served as a judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and as magistrate of Yongcheng County, where his governance won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 他邑訟不決者，郡守皇甫選輒屬億治之。

translations.literal: When lawsuits in other districts could not be resolved, the prefect Huangfu Xuan would invariably assign them to Yi to adjudicate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever cases elsewhere in the prefecture proved intractable, Prefect Huangfu Xuan routinely referred them to Yi for resolution.

sentences.zh: 通判陳州，會河決，治堤費萬計，億不賦民而營築之。

translations.literal: As vice-prefect of Chenzhou, when the river burst its banks, the cost of repairing the dikes ran to tens of thousands; Yi did not levy the people but undertook the construction himself.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as vice-prefect of Chenzhou, he faced a river breach whose dike repairs would cost tens of thousands of cash; rather than tax the populace, he organized and funded the work himself.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗欲召試，而與王旦有親嫌，特召見，改一官知洋州。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong once wished to summon him for an examination, but because he had a kinship conflict with Wang Dan, he was specially summoned for an audience, promoted one rank, and appointed prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong had intended to call him for a palace examination, but a marital tie to Wang Dan barred that route; instead the emperor granted him a special audience, raised his rank one step, and sent him to govern Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 州豪李甲，兄死迫嫂使嫁，因誣其子為他姓，以專其貲。

translations.literal: A local magnate named Li Jia, after his elder brother died, forced his sister-in-law to remarry and falsely claimed her son was of another surname in order to seize the family property.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful local named Li Jia, after his elder brother's death, coerced his sister-in-law into remarriage and falsely declared her son belonged to another clan so he could seize the estate.

sentences.zh: 嫂訴於官，甲輒賂吏掠服之，積十餘年，訴不已。

translations.literal: The sister-in-law sued in court, but Jia repeatedly bribed clerks to coerce her into submission; for more than ten years she kept appealing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: She brought the case to the authorities, yet Jia repeatedly bribed court clerks to intimidate her into yielding; for more than a decade she kept filing appeals.

sentences.zh: 億視舊牘未嘗引乳醫為證，召甲出乳醫示之，甲亡以為辭，冤遂辨。

translations.literal: Yi examined the old case files and saw that no wet-nurse physician had ever been cited as evidence; he summoned Jia and produced the wet nurse before him, and Jia had no further argument—the injustice was then cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reviewed the old dossiers and noticed that no wet nurse had ever been called as witness; he summoned Jia and presented the nurse to him, leaving Jia with nothing left to say, and the wrong was finally righted.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書屯田員外郎、知相州。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Field-Affairs Bureau and appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to become an assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue's field-affairs bureau and was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 河北旱，轉運使不以實聞，億獨言歲饑，願貸民租。

translations.literal: Hebei suffered drought; the transport commissioner did not report the true conditions, but Yi alone stated that the year was famine-stricken and asked to lend grain tax to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck Hebei, the transport commissioner concealed the severity of the crisis; Yi alone reported famine conditions and petitioned to defer the people's grain-tax payments.

sentences.zh: 有誣其子綱請求受金者，億請自置獄按之，事雖辨，猶降通判大名府。

translations.literal: Someone falsely accused his son Gang of soliciting and accepting gold; Yi asked to set up a prison himself to investigate, and though the matter was cleared, he was still demoted to vice-prefect of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Gang was falsely accused of taking bribes, Yi requested permission to conduct the inquiry in a prison under his own supervision; although Gang was cleared, Yi was nevertheless demoted to vice-prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 尋為殿中侍御史，遷侍御史，安撫淮、浙，除開封府判官，出為河北轉運使。

translations.literal: Soon he became a palace censor, was promoted to investigating censor, pacified Huai and Zhe, was appointed a judge of the Kaifeng prefectural court, and went out as transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became a palace censor, then an investigating censor, served as pacification commissioner for Huai and Zhe, was named a judge in the Kaifeng prefectural court, and finally was posted as Hebei transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，進直史館、知青州，以司封員外郎兼侍御史知雜事，判大理寺丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renzong's reign he entered the Historiography Institute as a compiler, governed Qingzhou, served as an assistant director in the Ministry of Rites' Seals Bureau while concurrently holding the post of supervising investigating censor, and judged cases as a vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Renzong's reign he joined the Historiography Institute, governed Qingzhou, and served as an assistant director in the Ministry of Rites while also supervising the censorate's routine business and hearing cases as a vice-director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 吳植知臨江軍，使人納金於宰相王欽若，因牙吏至京師，審之，語頗泄，欽若知不可掩，執吏以聞。

translations.literal: Wu Zhi, military prefect of Linjiang, sent someone to present gold to the chief minister Wang Qinruo; the matter reached the capital through a clerk, and upon investigation the story leaked considerably; Qinruo knew it could not be concealed and detained the clerk to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhi, prefect of Linjiang Circuit, had an agent deliver gold to Chief Minister Wang Qinruo; when a clerk brought the case to the capital and inquiries began, word spread widely; realizing the affair could not be hidden, Qinruo detained the clerk and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 詔付臺治，而植自言未嘗納金，反誣吏誤以問所親語達欽若。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the censorate to try the case, but Zhi himself declared he had never presented gold and instead accused the clerk of mistakenly conveying words he had asked a close associate to Qinruo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the censorate to investigate, but Zhi insisted he had never sent gold and accused the clerk of misreporting a private inquiry he had made to a confidant of Qinruo's.

sentences.zh: 億窮治之，蓋植以病懼廢，金未達而事已露也。

translations.literal: Yi pursued the investigation to the end; in fact Zhi, fearing removal because of illness, had sent the gold, but it had not arrived before the affair was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi pursued the case to its conclusion and found that Zhi, anxious about dismissal on account of illness, had indeed sent the bribe, though the gold never reached its destination before the plot came to light.

sentences.zh: 植乃除名，並按欽若，詔釋不問。

translations.literal: Zhi was then stripped of his name from the rolls, and Qinruo was investigated as well, but an edict ordered that he be released without prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was struck from the official rolls, and proceedings were opened against Qinruo as well, but an imperial edict ordered that he be released without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 三司更茶法，歲課不登，億承詔劾之，由丞相而下皆坐失當之罰，其不撓如此。

translations.literal: The Three Departments revised the tea law, but the year's revenue targets were not met; Yi received an edict to impeach those responsible, and from the chief councillor downward all were punished for impropriety—such was his refusal to yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Departments revised the tea monopoly and annual revenues fell short, Yi was ordered to investigate; from the chief councillor down, officials were penalized for mismanagement—such was his steadfastness in office.

sentences.zh: 自薛奎後，億獨掌臺務者逾年。

translations.literal: After Xue Kui, Yi alone managed censorate affairs for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Kui left office, Yi was the sole official directing censorate business for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 除龍圖閣待制，奉使契丹。

translations.literal: He was appointed a Hanlin academician-expositor in the Dragon Diagram Hall and sent on a mission to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an academician-expositor of the Dragon Diagram Hall and dispatched on an embassy to the Khitan court.

sentences.zh: 時副使者，章獻外姻也，妄傳皇太后旨於契丹，諭以南北歡好傳示子孫之意，億初不知也。

translations.literal: At the time the deputy envoy was a relative by marriage of Empress Dowager Zhang Xian; he falsely conveyed the empress dowager's instructions to the Khitan, telling them of the wish that north and south friendship be passed down to posterity—Yi did not know of this at first.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy envoy was a kinsman by marriage of Empress Dowager Zhang Xian; without authority he told the Khitan of the empress dowager's wish that the friendship of the two courts endure for generations—Yi knew nothing of this at first.

sentences.zh: 契丹主問億曰：「皇太后即有旨，大使何獨不言？」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler asked Yi, "If the empress dowager already has instructions, why does the chief envoy alone not speak of them?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler asked Yi, "If the empress dowager has already given her instructions, why has the chief envoy said nothing of them?"

sentences.zh: 億對曰：「本朝每遣使，皇太后必以此戒之，非欲達於北朝也。」

translations.literal: Yi replied, "Whenever our court dispatches envoys, the empress dowager always admonishes them in this way; it is not meant to be conveyed to the northern court."
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "Whenever our court sends envoys abroad, the empress dowager always offers them this counsel as a private admonition; it is not meant to be relayed to the northern court."

sentences.zh: 契丹主大喜，曰：「此兩朝生靈之福也。」

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased and said, "This is a blessing for the peoples of both courts."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was delighted and said, "This is a blessing for the peoples of both realms."

sentences.zh: 人謂副使既失辭，而億更以為恩意，甚推美之。

translations.literal: People said the deputy had already misspoken, yet Yi turned it instead into an expression of goodwill and was greatly praised for it.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said the deputy had already blundered in his remarks, yet Yi reframed the episode as a gesture of goodwill and won wide admiration for his tact.

sentences.zh: 知亳州，召知審刑院，再遷兵部郎中、同判吏部流內銓，以右諫議大夫、樞密直學士知益州。

translations.literal: He governed Bozhou, was summoned to direct the Court for Review of Punishments, was promoted again to a director in the Ministry of War and concurrent judge of the Ministry of Personnel's roster bureau, and was appointed prefect of Yizhou with the titles of Right Remonstrance Councillor and Academician Direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Bozhou, was recalled to head the Court for Review of Punishments, rose to director in the Ministry of War while also helping judge appointments in the Ministry of Personnel, and was sent to Yizhou as prefect with the rank of Right Remonstrance Councillor and as a direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 故事，益州歲出官粟六萬石，振糶貧民。

translations.literal: By precedent, Yizhou each year released sixty thousand bushels of government grain to sell cheaply to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, Yizhou each year released sixty thousand bushels of government grain for relief sales to the poor.

sentences.zh: 是歲大旱，億倍數出粟，先期予民，民坐是不饑。

translations.literal: That year there was severe drought; Yi released grain several times the usual amount and distributed it to the people ahead of schedule, so that because of this the people did not go hungry.
translations.idiomatic: That year a severe drought struck; Yi released several times the usual allotment of grain and distributed it to the people ahead of schedule, so the region escaped famine.

sentences.zh: 又疏九升江口，下溉民田數千頃。

translations.literal: He also dredged the mouth of the Jiushui River, irrigating several thousand qing of farmland downstream.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged the mouth of the Jiushui River, bringing irrigation to several thousand qing of farmland below.

sentences.zh: 維、茂州地接羌夷，蕃部歲至永康官場鬻馬，億慮其覘兩川，奏徙場黎州境上。

translations.literal: Wei and Mao prefectures bordered the Qiang and Yi peoples; each year tribal groups came to the Yongkang government horse market to sell horses; Yi feared they were reconnoitering the Two River regions and memorialized to move the market to the border of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Mao prefectures lay adjacent to Qiang and Yi territory; each year tribal groups came to the Yongkang government horse fair, and Yi, fearing they were scouting the Two Rivers region, petitioned to relocate the market to Lizhou's frontier.

sentences.zh: 拜御史中丞，請如唐制，置御史裏行。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and requested, following Tang institutions, to establish the post of censor trainee.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed vice censor-in-chief, he asked that the Tang practice of censor trainees be restored.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，以尚書工部侍郎同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou he served as Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Works and concurrently managed affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jingyou era (1035), he served as vice minister of works while also jointly directing the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時承平久，武備不戒，乃請二府各列上才任將帥者數十人，稍試用之。

translations.literal: At the time peace had lasted long and military preparations were neglected; he therefore asked both councils each to submit lists of dozens of men talented and fit for command, to be tried out gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that military readiness had lapsed; he asked both executive councils to nominate dozens of men of proven talent for command and to give them trial appointments.

sentences.zh: 又言武臣宜知兵，而書禁不傳，請纂其要授之。

translations.literal: He also said military officers ought to understand warfare, but prohibited books were not circulated; he asked to compile their essentials and grant them.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that military officers ought to know the art of war, yet restricted texts were not circulated to them; he petitioned to compile their essentials and distribute them.

sentences.zh: 於是帝親集《神武秘略》，以賜邊臣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor personally compiled the Secret Essentials of Divine Military Affairs and bestowed it on frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon personally compiled the Secret Essentials of Divine Military Affairs and presented it to frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 唃廝囉與趙元昊相攻，來獻捷。

translations.literal: Gusiluo and Zhao Yuanhao attacked each other and came to present reports of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo and Zhao Yuanhao were at war with each other and sent word of their victories to the court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議加唃廝囉節制，億曰：「彼皆蕃臣也，今不能諭令解仇，乃因而加賞，非所以綏御四方也。」

translations.literal: The court discussed adding Gusiluo to the military commission system; Yi said, "They are all tribal subjects; now we cannot instruct them to end their feud yet reward them for it—this is not the way to pacify and control the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated elevating Gusiluo with a military commission, Yi said, "They are all tribal subjects under the throne; we cannot even persuade them to end their feud, yet we would reward one of them for fighting the other—that is no way to pacify the realm."

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 元昊歲遣人至京師，出入民間無他禁，億請下詔為除館舍禮之，官主貿易，外雖若煩擾，實羈防之。

translations.literal: Each year Yuanhao sent people to the capital who moved freely among the populace without other restriction; Yi asked that an edict be issued to set aside lodgings and receive them with ceremony, with officials supervising trade—outwardly it seemed troublesome, but in fact it restrained and guarded against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao each year sent envoys to the capital who mingled freely among the populace; Yi petitioned for an edict establishing guest quarters and formal reception, with officials supervising their trade—though it seemed burdensome on the surface, it was in fact a means of control.

sentences.zh: 知開封府范仲淹獻《百官圖》，指宰相呂夷簡差除不平，而陰薦億可用。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan, who governed Kaifeng Prefecture, presented the Chart of the Hundred Officials, pointing out that Chief Minister Lü Yijian's appointments were unfair, while secretly recommending Yi as usable.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan, prefect of Kaifeng, submitted the Chart of the Hundred Officials, accusing Chief Minister Lü Yijian of partisan appointments while quietly recommending Yi as a capable replacement.

sentences.zh: 仲淹既貶，帝以諭億，億曰：「仲淹舉臣以公，臣之愚陛下所知；

translations.literal: After Zhongyan was demoted, the emperor informed Yi of this; Yi said, "Zhongyan recommended me on public grounds—Your Majesty knows my inadequacies;
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongyan's demotion, the emperor told Yi of the recommendation; Yi replied, "If Zhongyan recommended me on public grounds, Your Majesty already knows my limitations;

sentences.zh: 舉臣以私，則臣委質以來，未嘗交託於人。」

translations.literal: if he recommended me on private grounds, then since I pledged my service I have never entrusted myself to anyone."
translations.idiomatic: but if he did so for private reasons, then since I entered your service I have never cultivated such patronage ties."

sentences.zh: 遂除戶部、參知政事。

translations.literal: He was then appointed to the Ministry of Revenue and made a Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon appointed to the Ministry of Revenue and made a vice grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 會忻州地大震，諫官韓琦言宰相王隨、陳堯佐非輔弼才，又言億子綜為群牧判官，不當自請以兄綱代之。

translations.literal: When a great earthquake struck Xinzhou, remonstrance official Han Qi said that chief ministers Wang Sui and Chen Yaozuo were not fit to assist and govern, and also said that Yi's son Zong, a judge of the Directorate of Horse Pasturages, ought not to have asked on his own to replace his elder brother Gang.
translations.idiomatic: When a major earthquake struck Xinzhou, Remonstrance Official Han Qi declared that Chief Ministers Wang Sui and Chen Yaozuo were unfit for high office, and also objected that Yi's son Zong, a judge in the Directorate of Horse Pasturages, had improperly petitioned to replace his elder brother Gang.

sentences.zh: 遂與宰相皆罷，知應天府，尋加資政殿學士、知成德軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and the chief ministers were all dismissed; he governed Yingtian Prefecture, and soon was given the title of Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and appointed military prefect of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: He and the chief ministers were all dismissed; he was sent to govern Yingtian Prefecture, and soon was made an academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and military prefect of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 改澶州，復知亳州，官至尚書左丞，以太子少傅致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chunzhou, again governed Bozhou, rose to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chunzhou, returned to govern Bozhou, rose to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and retired with the title of junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，諡「忠憲」。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title "Loyal and Law-abiding."
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the court posthumously honored him as grand tutor to the heir apparent and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Law-abiding.

sentences.zh: 億性方重，治家嚴飭，雖燕居，未嘗有惰容。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was upright and grave; he governed his household with strict discipline, and even in leisurely repose never showed a negligent bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was upright and grave by nature, ran his household with strict discipline, and even in private leisure never showed a negligent demeanor.

sentences.zh: 見親舊之孤貧者，常給其昏葬。

translations.literal: When he saw relatives and old friends who were orphaned and poor, he regularly provided for their weddings and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he encountered impoverished relatives and old friends, he regularly helped pay for their weddings and funerals.

sentences.zh: 每見天下諸路有奏攟拾官吏小過者，輒顏色不懌，曰：「天下太平，聖主之心，雖昆蟲草木，皆欲使之得所。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw memorials from circuits throughout the realm picking out minor faults of officials, his expression would turn displeased, and he would say, "The realm is at peace; the sage ruler's heart wishes that even insects and plants each find their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw memorials from across the empire nitpicking minor faults of officials, his face would cloud over, and he would say, "The realm is at peace; the sage ruler's heart desires that even the smallest creatures each find their proper place.

sentences.zh: 今仕者大則望為公卿，次亦望為侍從、職司一千石，其下亦望京朝、幕職，奈何錮之於盛世？」

translations.literal: Now officials at the highest hope to become chief ministers, those next hope to become attendants-in-waiting or thousand-bushel administrators, and those below still hope for capital posts or staff appointments—why confine them in an age of splendor?"
translations.idiomatic: Officials at the top aspire to chief ministerships, those in the middle to court attendant posts or prefectural office, and those below even to capital staff appointments—why shackle them in an age of prosperity?"

sentences.zh: 八子：綱、綜、絳、繹、維、縝、緯、緬。

translations.literal: He had eight sons: Gang, Zong, Jiang, Yi, Wei, Zhen, Wei, and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons: Gang, Zong, Jiang, Yi, Wei, Zhen, Wei, and Mian.

sentences.zh: 綱，尚書水部員外郎。

translations.literal: Gang served as an assistant director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Gang held the post of assistant director in the Ministry of Works' Water Bureau.

sentences.zh: 慶歷中，知光化軍，性苛急，不能撫循士卒。

translations.literal: During the Qingli era he governed Guanghua Army; his nature was harsh and impatient, and he could not comfort and guide the troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era he commanded Guanghua Army; harsh and impatient by nature, he failed to win the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 會盜張海剽劫至境上，綱帥禁兵乘城，給餅餌多不時，民具酒食犒軍，輒收其羊豕，市錢制兵器，士皆憤怒。

translations.literal: When the bandit Zhang Hai raided to the border, Gang led the palace troops onto the walls; rations of cakes were often not delivered on time; when the people prepared wine and food to reward the army, he would seize their sheep and pigs, sell them for cash to make weapons, and the soldiers were all furious.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit Zhang Hai raided the borderlands, Gang led the palace troops onto the walls; he often delivered rations late, and when civilians brought wine and food to reward the troops, he seized their livestock, sold it for cash to buy weapons, and the soldiers grew furious.

sentences.zh: 又嘗命軍校作陣圖，不成，將斬之，眾益駭。

translations.literal: He also once ordered a military officer to draw up a battle formation diagram; when it was not completed he was about to execute him, and the crowd grew still more terrified.
translations.idiomatic: He once ordered an officer to draft a battle formation diagram; when the man failed, Gang was about to execute him, and the troops were further alarmed.

sentences.zh: 一日，士方食，軍校邵興叱眾起勿食。

translations.literal: One day, while the soldiers were eating, the military officer Shao Xing shouted at the crowd to rise and not eat.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as the men were eating, the officer Shao Xing shouted for them to rise and stop eating.

sentences.zh: 綱怒，執數人繫獄。

translations.literal: Gang was enraged and seized several men and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Gang flew into a rage, seized several men, and threw them in prison.

sentences.zh: 興懼，帥眾劫庫兵為亂，欲殺綱。

translations.literal: Xing feared for himself, led the crowd to seize arsenal weapons and rebel, and intended to kill Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xing led the men to seize weapons from the arsenal and mutiny, intending to kill Gang.

sentences.zh: 綱攜妻子縋城，由漢江而下。

translations.literal: Gang took his wife and children and lowered himself by rope from the wall, going down the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Gang lowered his wife and children over the wall by rope and fled down the Han River.

sentences.zh: 興等遂縱火掠城中，引眾趨蜀道，為官兵所敗，遂斬之，余黨悉誅。

translations.literal: Xing and the others then set fires and plundered within the city, led the crowd toward the road to Shu, were defeated by government troops, and were then executed; the remaining partisans were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xing and his followers set fires and looted the city, then marched toward Shu; government troops defeated them, executed Xing, and put all the remaining rebels to death.

sentences.zh: 綱坐棄城除名，編管英州。

translations.literal: Gang, on account of abandoning the city, was struck from the rolls and placed under registered supervision in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was struck from the rolls for abandoning his post and was placed under registered supervision in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子 綜

translations.literal: Son: Zong
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zong

sentences.zh: 綜，字仲文。

translations.literal: Zong, courtesy name Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, whose courtesy name was Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 蔭補將作監主簿，遷大理評事。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed a registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings and was promoted to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as a registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings and was promoted to judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 舉進士中第，通判鄧州、天雄軍。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as vice-prefect of Dengzhou and Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as vice-prefect of Dengzhou and Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 會河溢金堤，民依丘冢者數百家。

translations.literal: When the river overflowed the Jin Embankment, several hundred households of people took refuge on mounds and tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When the river breached the Jin Embankment, several hundred families took refuge on burial mounds and hillocks.

sentences.zh: 綜令曰：「能濟一人，予千錢。」

translations.literal: Zong issued an order saying, "Whoever can rescue one person will receive a thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: Zong proclaimed, "Whoever rescues one person shall receive a thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 民爭操舟筏以救，已而丘冢多潰。

translations.literal: The people competed to take boats and rafts to save them, and before long many of the mounds and tombs collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The people rushed to man boats and rafts to save them, and before long many of the mounds collapsed.

sentences.zh: 呂夷簡自北京入相，薦為集賢校理、同知太常院。

translations.literal: When Lü Yijian entered the chief ministership from Beijing, he recommended him as collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents and concurrent vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yijian came from Beijing to become chief minister, he recommended Zong as collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents and vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官，數月，遷三司戶部判官、同修起居注。

translations.literal: He served as an investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture; within several months he was promoted to judge of the Revenue Bureau in the Three Departments and compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an investigating officer in Kaifeng Prefecture and within months was promoted to judge in the Three Departments' Revenue Bureau and compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，契丹主問其家世，綜言億在先朝嘗持禮來，契丹主喜曰：「與中國通好久，父子俱使我，宜酌我酒。」

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan, the Khitan ruler asked about his family background; Zong said that Yi in the previous reign had once come bearing ritual propriety, and the Khitan ruler said with pleasure, "We have been in contact with China for so long—father and son both serving as my envoys—you ought to toast my wine."
translations.idiomatic: On an embassy to the Khitan, the ruler asked about his lineage; Zong replied that his father Yi had once come on embassy in the previous reign, and the Khitan ruler said delightedly, "We have dealt with China for so long—father and son both serving as my envoys—you ought to toast me."

sentences.zh: 綜率同使者五人起為壽，契丹主亦離席酬之，歡甚。

translations.literal: Zong led the five fellow envoys to rise and offer a toast; the Khitan ruler also left his seat to return the courtesy, and the merriment was great.
translations.idiomatic: Zong led the five fellow envoys in rising to offer a toast; the Khitan ruler left his seat to return the courtesy, and the banquet was exceedingly merry.

sentences.zh: 既還，陳執中以為生事，出知滑州，徙許州。

translations.literal: After returning, Chen Zhizhong regarded it as stirring up trouble and sent him out to govern Huazhou, then transferred him to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his return, Chen Zhizhong deemed the affair provocative and sent him out to govern Huazhou, then transferred him to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 殿前指揮使許懷德從妹亡，有別產在陽翟，以無子，籍於官，懷德欲私有之，訟未決。

translations.literal: Commander of the Palace Front Guard Xu Huaide's younger cousin by marriage died; there was separate property in Yangdi; because there were no sons it was registered with the government; Huaide wished to seize it privately, and the lawsuit was unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Xu Huaide's younger cousin-in-law died leaving separate property in Yangdi; with no heirs it was registered as state property, and Huaide sought to seize it for himself, but the suit remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 因楊儀為書屬綜，書至而轉運使已徙獄他州矣。

translations.literal: Through Yang Yi he wrote a letter entrusting it to Zong; when the letter arrived the transport commissioner had already moved the case to another prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yang Yi write to Zong on his behalf; by the time the letter arrived the transport commissioner had already transferred the case to another prefecture.

sentences.zh: 綜坐得書不以聞，奪集賢校理，知袁州。

translations.literal: Zong was punished for receiving the letter and not reporting it; he was stripped of his collatorship in the Hall of Assembled Talents and appointed prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was punished for receiving the letter without reporting it, stripped of his collatorship, and sent to govern Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為江東轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made transport commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as transport commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 還，再修起居注，累遷刑部員外郎、知制誥，卒。

translations.literal: On returning he again compiled the Diary of Activity and Repose, was promoted in succession to assistant director in the Ministry of Justice and drafter of edicts, and died.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he again compiled the imperial diary, rose to assistant director in the Ministry of Justice and drafter of edicts, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 綜嘗為契丹館伴使，使者欲為書稱北朝而去契丹號。

translations.literal: Zong once served as Khitan reception envoy; the envoy wished to write in a letter calling them the Northern Court and omitting the Khitan name.
translations.idiomatic: Zong once served as reception envoy for Khitan embassies; an envoy wished to draft a letter calling them the Northern Court while omitting the Khitan designation.

sentences.zh: 綜曰：「自古未有建國而無號者。」

translations.literal: Zong said, "Since antiquity there has never been a state founded without a name."
translations.idiomatic: Zong replied, "Since antiquity no state has ever been founded without a formal name."

sentences.zh: 使慚，遂不復言。

translations.literal: The envoy was ashamed and spoke no more of it.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was shamed into silence.

sentences.zh: 其後朝廷擇館伴契丹使者，帝曰：「孰有如韓綜者乎？」

translations.literal: Later when the court chose reception envoys for Khitan missions, the emperor said, "Who is there like Han Zong?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the court chose reception envoys for Khitan missions, the emperor said, "Who is there to match Han Zong?"

sentences.zh: 子宗道，為戶部侍郎、寶文閣待制。

translations.literal: His son Zongdao served as Vice Minister of Revenue and Hanlin academician-expositor in the Hall of Treasured Literature.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongdao rose to vice minister of revenue and academician-expositor of the Hall of Treasured Literature.

sentences.zh: 綱子宗彥，字欽聖。

translations.literal: Gang's son Zongyan, courtesy name Qinsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gang's son Zongyan, whose courtesy name was Qinsheng.

sentences.zh: 蔭補將作監主簿。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as a registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the top class and was promoted in succession to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the top class and rose to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以大臣薦，召試，為集賢校理。

translations.literal: On recommendation of a chief minister he was summoned for examination and made collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by a chief minister, he was summoned for a palace examination and appointed collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents.

sentences.zh: 歷提點京西、京東刑獄。

translations.literal: He served in succession as judicial intendant for Jingxi and Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as judicial intendant for the Jingxi and Jingdong circuits.

sentences.zh: 應天府失入平民死罪，獄成未決，通判孫世寧辨正之。

translations.literal: In Yingtian Prefecture a commoner was wrongly sentenced to death; the case was completed but not yet decided, and Vice-Prefect Sun Shining corrected it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingtian Prefecture a commoner had been wrongly sentenced to death; though the case was complete, Vice-Prefect Sun Shining overturned the verdict.

sentences.zh: 獄吏當坐法，而尹劉沆縱弗治；

translations.literal: The prison clerks ought to have been punished by law, but Prefect Liu Kang let it go without prosecution;
translations.idiomatic: The prison clerks should have been punished by law, but Prefect Liu Kang declined to prosecute them;

sentences.zh: 宗彥往按舉，沆復沮止之。

translations.literal: Zongyan went to investigate and impeach, but Kang again obstructed and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan went to investigate and impeach, but Kang again blocked him.

sentences.zh: 宗彥疏沆於朝，抵吏罪。

translations.literal: Zongyan memorialized against Kang at court and brought the clerks to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan memorialized against Kang at court and secured punishment for the clerks.

sentences.zh: 仁宗春秋高，未有嗣。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was advanced in years and had no heir.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was advanced in years and still had no heir.

sentences.zh: 宗彥上書曰：「漢章帝詔諸懷妊者賜胎養穀，人三斗，復其夫勿算一歲，著為令。

translations.literal: Zongyan submitted a memorial saying, "Emperor Zhang of Han ordered that all who were pregnant be granted fetal-nourishment grain, three dou per person, and that their husbands be exempted from corvée for one year—this was established as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan submitted a memorial: "Emperor Zhang of Han decreed grain allowances for pregnant women—three dou each—and exempted their husbands from corvée for one year, establishing this as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 臣考尋世次，帝八子，長則和帝，而質、安以下諸帝皆其系胄，請修胎養之令。」

translations.literal: Your servant has examined the succession: the emperor had eight sons; the eldest was Emperor He, and the emperors from Zhi and An downward were all of his line—your servant asks to restore the fetal-nourishment statute."
translations.idiomatic: I have traced the succession: the emperor had eight sons; the eldest became Emperor He, and the emperors from Zhi and An onward were all his descendants—I petition to restore the fetal-nourishment statute."

sentences.zh: 且曰：「人君務蕃毓其民，則天亦昌衍其子孫矣。」

translations.literal: He also said, "When a ruler strives to multiply and nurture his people, Heaven also extends and multiplies his descendants."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "When a ruler strives to nurture and increase his people, Heaven in turn blesses and multiplies his descendants."

sentences.zh: 以尚書兵部員外郎判三司鹽鐵勾院，卒。

translations.literal: He served as assistant director in the Ministry of War's Military Bureau while judging the Salt and Iron Audit Office of the Three Departments, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant director in the Ministry of War while overseeing the Salt and Iron Audit Office of the Three Departments, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 綜子宗道，歷官至戶部侍郎、寶文閣待制。

translations.literal: Zong's son Zongdao rose through offices to Vice Minister of Revenue and Hanlin academician-expositor in the Hall of Treasured Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's son Zongdao rose through the ranks to vice minister of revenue and academician-expositor of the Hall of Treasured Literature.

sentences.zh: 韓絳，字子華。

translations.literal: Han Jiang, courtesy name Zihua.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang, whose courtesy name was Zihua.

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，通判陳州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the top class and served as vice-prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the top class and served as vice-prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 直集賢院，為開封府推官。

translations.literal: He was a compiler in the Hall of Assembled Talents and served as an investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a compiler in the Hall of Assembled Talents and as an investigating officer in Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有男子冷青，妄稱其母頃在掖庭得幸，有娠而出生己，府以為狂，奏流汝州。

translations.literal: There was a man named Leng Qing who falsely claimed that his mother had recently been favored in the palace women's quarters, became pregnant, and gave birth to him; the prefecture regarded him as mad and memorialized to exile him to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Leng Qing falsely claimed his mother had recently been favored in the palace women's quarters, conceived him there, and given birth to him; the prefectural court deemed him mad and petitioned to exile him to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 絳言，留之在外將惑眾。

translations.literal: Jiang said that keeping him outside would mislead the populace.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang argued that leaving him at large would mislead the public.

sentences.zh: 追責窮治，蓋其母嘗執役宮禁，嫁民冷緒，生一女，乃生青，遂論棄市。

translations.literal: He was pursued and investigated to the end; in fact his mother had once served in the palace precincts, married the commoner Leng Xu, bore a daughter, and then bore Qing—he was sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued and thoroughly investigated, the truth emerged: his mother had once served in the palace, married a commoner named Leng Xu, bore a daughter, then Qing—Qing was sentenced to public execution.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部判官。

translations.literal: He served as judge of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge in the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 江南飢，為體量安撫使，行便民事數十條；

translations.literal: When Jiangnan suffered famine, he was made assessment and pacification commissioner and enacted several dozen measures for the people's convenience;
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Jiangnan, he was appointed assessment and pacification commissioner and enacted dozens of relief measures for the people;

sentences.zh: 宣州守廖詢貪暴不法，下吏寘諸理，民大悅。

translations.literal: The prefect of Xuanzhou, Liao Xun, was greedy, violent, and lawless; Jiang sent subordinates to place him before the law, and the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhou Prefect Liao Xun was greedy, violent, and lawless; Jiang had him brought to justice, to the great delight of the people.

sentences.zh: 使還，同修起居注，擢右正言。

translations.literal: On returning from his mission he compiled the Diary of Activity and Repose and was promoted to Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: After his mission he helped compile the imperial diary and was promoted to Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 仁宗謂絳曰：「用卿出自朕，卿凡論事，不宜過激，當存朝廷大體，要令可行，毋使朕為不聽諫者。」

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said to Jiang, "I myself raised you to office; in all your remonstrances you ought not to be too extreme—you should preserve the great principles of the court, make proposals workable, and not make me appear one who refuses remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong told Jiang, "I personally elevated you; in your remonstrances you must not be excessive—preserve the court's larger interests, propose what can actually be done, and do not make me seem deaf to counsel."

sentences.zh: 入內都都知王守忠兼判內侍省，絳言：「判名太重，且國朝以來，未有兼判兩省者。」

translations.literal: Wang Shouzhong, Director of the Inner Palace Service, was also made concurrent administrator of the Directorate of Palace Attendants; Jiang said, "The title of administrator is too weighty, and since the founding of our dynasty there has never been one who concurrently administered two directorates."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shouzhong, Director of the Inner Palace Service, was also made concurrent administrator of the Directorate of Palace Attendants, Jiang objected: "The title is too weighty, and since our dynasty's founding no one has concurrently administered two directorates."

sentences.zh: 詔自今勿復除。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from now on such appointments should not be made again.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade such appointments in future.

sentences.zh: 道士趙清貺出入宰相龐籍家，以賂敗，開封杖流之，道死。

translations.literal: The Daoist Zhao Qingban frequented Chief Minister Pang Ji's household; exposed for bribery, Kaifeng had him beaten with the cudgel and exiled, and he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Zhao Qingban frequented Chief Minister Pang Ji's home; exposed for bribery, Kaifeng had him beaten and exiled, and he died en route.

sentences.zh: 絳言籍諷府殺之，籍與尹俱謫去。

translations.literal: Jiang said Ji had prompted the prefecture to kill him; Ji and the prefect were both demoted and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang charged that Ji had prompted the prefectural court to kill him; both Ji and the prefect were demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 未幾復進，絳力爭不得，遂解言職。

translations.literal: Before long Ji was promoted again; Jiang strove against it but could not prevail, and thereupon resigned his remonstrance post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ji was promoted again; Jiang fought the appointment in vain and resigned his remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 明年，知制誥，乞守河陽，召判流內銓。

translations.literal: The next year he was made drafter of edicts, requested to guard Heyang, and was summoned to judge the roster bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became drafter of edicts, requested a post guarding Heyang, and was recalled to judge appointments in the roster bureau.

sentences.zh: 河決商胡，用李仲昌議，開六塔河而患滋甚，命絳安撫河北。

translations.literal: The river breached at Shanghu; following Li Zhongchang's proposal the Liuta River was opened, yet the calamity grew worse; Jiang was ordered to pacify Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River breached at Shanghu, Li Zhongchang's plan to open the Liuta channel only worsened the disaster; Jiang was ordered to pacify Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時宰主仲昌，人莫敢異。

translations.literal: The chief minister at the time championed Zhongchang, and no one dared dissent.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister backed Zhongchang, and no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 絳劾其蠹國害民，罪不可貸，仲昌遂竄嶺表。

translations.literal: Jiang impeached him for harming the state and injuring the people, his crime unpardonable; Zhongchang was then banished to the Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang impeached him for ruining the state and harming the people, declaring his crime unpardonable; Zhongchang was banished to the far south.

sentences.zh: 遷龍圖閣直學士、知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin academician-direct of the Dragon Diagram Hall and appointed prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician-direct of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修率同列言：「絳宜在朝廷，瀛非所處也。」

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu led his colleagues in saying, "Jiang ought to be at court; Ying is not where he belongs."
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu led his colleagues in petitioning, "Jiang belongs at court; Yingzhou is no place for him."

sentences.zh: 留知諫院，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He was retained to direct the Remonstrance Bureau and to investigate capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept at court to direct the Remonstrance Bureau and oversee capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 為翰林學士、御史中丞。

translations.literal: He became a Hanlin academician and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Hanlin academician and vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 帝禱茅山求嗣，絳草祝辭，因勸帝汰出宮人，及限內臣養子，以重絕人之世，皆從之。

translations.literal: The emperor prayed at Mount Mao for an heir; Jiang drafted the prayer text and thereby urged the emperor to dismiss palace women and to limit palace attendants' adoption of sons, so as to emphasize the severity of a line without heirs—all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor prayed at Mount Mao for an heir, Jiang drafted the prayer and urged him to release palace women and limit eunuchs' adoptions of sons, stressing the gravity of dynastic extinction—the emperor accepted all his advice.

sentences.zh: 掖庭劉氏通請謁為奸，絳以告帝，帝曰：「非卿言，朕無由知。」

translations.literal: Liu of the palace women's quarters had illicit relations through requests for audience; Jiang reported this to the emperor, who said, "Had you not spoken, I would have had no way to know."
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the palace quarters surnamed Liu had been conducting illicit affairs through petitioned audiences; Jiang reported this to the emperor, who said, "Without your report, I would never have known."

sentences.zh: 不數日，出劉氏及他不謹者。

translations.literal: Within a few days Liu and others who were not circumspect were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Liu and other offenders were expelled from the palace.

sentences.zh: 真定守呂溱犯法，從官通章請貰之，絳曰：「法行當自貴者始，更相請援，則公道廢矣。」

translations.literal: The prefect of Zhending, Lü Zhen, violated the law; attendant officials jointly memorialized asking pardon for him; Jiang said, "When law is enforced it should begin with the exalted; if they keep pleading for one another, public justice is abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Zhending Prefect Lü Zhen broke the law, and court attendants jointly petitioned for his pardon; Jiang said, "Law must be applied first to the highest ranks; if officials keep interceding for one another, public justice is finished."

sentences.zh: 並劾諸請者，溱遂絀。

translations.literal: He also impeached all who had petitioned, and Zhen was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached all who had petitioned, and Zhen was demoted.

sentences.zh: 富弼用張茂實掌禁兵，絳言：「人謂茂實為先帝子，豈宜用典宿衛？」

translations.literal: Fu Bi employed Zhang Maoshi to command the palace guard; Jiang said, "People say Maoshi is a son of the late emperor—how can he be used to oversee the inner guard?"
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Bi appointed Zhang Maoshi to command the palace guard, Jiang objected, "People say Maoshi is a son of the late emperor—how can he be placed in charge of the inner guard?"

sentences.zh: 不報，闔門待罪，自言不敢復稱御史中丞。

translations.literal: There was no response; he closed his gates and awaited punishment, declaring he dared no longer style himself Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond; Jiang shut his gates and awaited punishment, declaring he could no longer hold the title of vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 詔召之，及出，不秉笏穿朝堂，諫官論之，罷知蔡州。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him; when he came out he crossed the court hall without holding his tablet; remonstrance officials criticized this, and he was dismissed to govern Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him back, but when he appeared he crossed the court hall without holding his ceremonial tablet; remonstrance officials censured him, and he was sent to govern Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 數月，以翰林侍讀學士知慶州。

translations.literal: Several months later he was made Hanlin attendant reader and appointed to govern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was made Hanlin attendant reader and sent to govern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 熟羌據堡為亂，即日討平之。

translations.literal: Acculturated Qiang held forts in rebellion; on the same day he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Acculturated Qiang rebels seized frontier forts; he suppressed them the same day.

sentences.zh: 加端明殿學士、知成都府。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and appointed prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an academician of the Hall of Brilliant Governance and appointed prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 張詠鎮蜀日，春糶米，秋糶鹽，官給券以惠貧弱，歷歲久，權歸豪右；

translations.literal: When Zhang Yong governed Shu, in spring grain was sold cheap, in autumn salt was sold cheap, and the government issued vouchers to benefit the poor and weak; over many years power passed to the great families;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yong governed Shu, the government sold grain cheaply in spring and salt cheaply in autumn, issuing vouchers to aid the poor; over the years control passed to powerful local families;

sentences.zh: 中人奉使至蜀，使酒吏主貿易，因附益以取悅，絳悉奏罷之。

translations.literal: Palace envoys sent on missions to Shu had wine clerks manage trade and added profits to please others; Jiang memorialized to abolish all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys to Shu had wine clerks manage trade and skim profits to curry favor; Jiang memorialized to abolish the practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 召知開封府，為三司使。

translations.literal: He was summoned to govern Kaifeng Prefecture and made commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Kaifeng and appointed commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 請以川、陝職田穀輸常平倉，而隨其事任道里差次給直。

translations.literal: He asked that grain from official fields in Chuan and Shan be delivered to the Ever-Normal Granary, with payment given according to the duties involved and the distance in stages.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed delivering grain from official fields in Sichuan and Shaanxi to the Ever-Normal Granary, with payment scaled to duties and distance.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆曰：「眾方姑息，卿獨不能徇時邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said, "Everyone is indulgent and accommodating—can you alone not follow the times?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "Everyone else is indulgent—must you alone refuse to bend with the times?"

sentences.zh: 即行之。

translations.literal: It was immediately put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was immediately implemented.

sentences.zh: 內諸司吏數干恩澤，絳輒執不可。

translations.literal: Clerks of the inner bureaus repeatedly sought favors, and Jiang invariably held firm and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks of the inner bureaus repeatedly sought favors, and Jiang invariably refused.

sentences.zh: 為帝言：「身犯眾怒，懼有飛語。」

translations.literal: He told the emperor, "I have incurred the wrath of many and fear there will be slanderous reports."
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, "I have incurred widespread anger and fear slander will follow."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕在藩邸日，頗聞有司以國事為人情。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "When I was in my princely residence I often heard that officials treated state affairs as personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "When I was still a prince I often heard officials treat state business as personal favor-trading.

sentences.zh: 卿所守固善，何憚於讒？」

translations.literal: What you uphold is indeed good—why fear slander?"
translations.idiomatic: What you uphold is right—why fear slander?"

sentences.zh: 神宗立，韓琦薦絳有公輔器，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong ascended, Han Qi recommended that Jiang had the capacity of a chief minister and he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong ascended, Han Qi recommended Jiang as chief-minister material, and he was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 始請建審官西院，掌武臣升朝者，以息吏奸。

translations.literal: He first requested establishing the Western Bureau for Review of Appointments to manage military officers promoted to court attendance, in order to curb clerical corruption.
translations.idiomatic: He first proposed establishing the Western Bureau for Review of Appointments to oversee military officers promoted to court attendance, in order to curb clerical abuses.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘗問天下遺利，絳請盡地力。

translations.literal: Shenzong once asked about unexploited profits throughout the realm; Jiang asked to exhaust the land's productive power.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong asked about untapped revenues throughout the realm, Jiang urged fully exploiting the land's productive capacity.

sentences.zh: 因言差役之弊，願更定其法，役議自此始矣。

translations.literal: He thereby spoke of the abuses of corvée assignment and wished to revise its regulations—debate over corvée reform began from this.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of the abuses of the corvée-assignment system and petitioned to revise its regulations—debate over corvée reform began here.

sentences.zh: 代陳升之同制置三司條例，王安石每奏事，必曰：「臣見安石所陳非一，皆至當可用，陛下宜省察。」

translations.literal: Replacing Chen Shengzhi, he jointly directed the Three Departments regulations; whenever Wang Anshi memorialized, Jiang would invariably say, "Your servant has seen that what Anshi presents, though not single, is all most fitting and usable—Your Majesty should examine it."
translations.idiomatic: Replacing Chen Shengzhi, he jointly directed the Three Departments regulations; whenever Wang Anshi memorialized, Jiang would say, "Everything Anshi proposes is sound and practicable—Your Majesty should give it careful attention."

sentences.zh: 安石恃以為助。

translations.literal: Anshi relied on him as a supporter.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi counted on him as an ally.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining he became Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xining era (1070) he became vice grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯塞，絳請行邊，安石亦請往。

translations.literal: The Xia people raided the border; Jiang requested to go to the frontier, and Anshi also requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut Xia raided the border, Jiang volunteered to go to the frontier, and Anshi did likewise.

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「朝廷方賴安石，臣宜行。」

translations.literal: Jiang said, "The court now relies on Anshi—I ought to go."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "The court depends on Anshi—I should go instead."

sentences.zh: 乃以為陝西宣撫使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon made pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly appointed pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 既又兼河東，幾事不可待報者，聽便宜施行，授以空名告敕，得自除吏。

translations.literal: He was then also given charge of Hedong; matters that could not await reports were permitted to be handled as expedients; he was granted blank commission documents and could appoint officials on his own.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given charge of Hedong; urgent matters could be handled without awaiting court approval; he received blank commission documents and authority to appoint officials on his own.

sentences.zh: 十二月，即軍中拜同中書門下平章事、昭文館大學士，開幕府於延安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, right in the army he was appointed Associate Grand Councillor of the Tongzhongshu Menxia type and Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, and opened a staff headquarters at Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was appointed associate grand councillor and grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall right in camp, and established his headquarters at Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 絳素不習兵事，注措乖方，選蕃兵為七軍，用知青澗城种諤策，欲取橫山，令諸將聽命於諤，厚賞犒蕃兵，眾皆怨望；

translations.literal: Jiang had never been versed in military affairs; his arrangements were ill-suited; he selected tribal troops into seven armies, adopted the stratagem of Chong E, who knew Qingjian Fort, to take Hengshan, ordered all generals to obey E, and richly rewarded and feasted the tribal soldiers—everyone resented this;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang had no military experience; his arrangements were misguided; he organized tribal troops into seven armies, adopted Chong E of Qingjian Fort's plan to seize Hengshan, ordered all generals to obey E, and lavished rewards on tribal soldiers—to widespread resentment;

sentences.zh: 又奪騎兵馬以與之，有抱馬首以泣者。

translations.literal: He also seized cavalry horses to give to them; some clutched their horses' heads and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized cavalry horses to give them, and some soldiers clutched their horses' heads and wept.

sentences.zh: 既城囉兀，又冒雪築撫寧堡，調發騷然。

translations.literal: After fortifying Luowu, he again built Funing Fort in the snow; levies and transport caused great turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: After fortifying Luowu, he built Funing Fort in the snow; conscription and transport threw the region into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 已而二城陷，趣諸道兵出援，慶卒遂作亂。

translations.literal: Before long both forts fell; he urged troops from all circuits to march out in relief, and the Qingzhou garrison then mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both forts fell; he urgently summoned troops from all circuits, and the Qingzhou garrison mutinied.

sentences.zh: 議者罪絳，罷知鄧州。

translations.literal: Critics blamed Jiang; he was dismissed to govern Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics blamed Jiang; he was dismissed and sent to govern Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，以觀文殿學士徙許州，進大學士，徙大名府。

translations.literal: The next year, as an academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature he was transferred to Xuzhou, advanced to Grand Academician, and transferred to Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Xuzhou as an academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, promoted to grand academician, and transferred to Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年，復代王安石相。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he again replaced Wang Anshi as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he again replaced Wang Anshi as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 既顓處中書，事多稽留不決，且數與呂惠卿爭論，乃密請帝再用安石。

translations.literal: Once he presided at the Secretariat, many matters were delayed without decision, and he repeatedly argued with Lü Huiqing; he then secretly asked the emperor to employ Anshi again.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the head of the Secretariat, he delayed many decisions and repeatedly clashed with Lü Huiqing; he then secretly asked the emperor to recall Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安石至，頗與絳異。

translations.literal: When Anshi arrived, he differed considerably from Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi returned, he and Jiang differed on many matters.

sentences.zh: 有劉佐者，坐法免，安石欲抆拭用佐，絳不可。

translations.literal: There was a Liu Zuo who had been dismissed for violating the law; Anshi wished to wipe away the stain and employ Zuo; Jiang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Liu Zuo had been dismissed for breaking the law; Anshi wished to rehabilitate and employ him; Jiang refused.

sentences.zh: 議帝前未決，即再拜求去。

translations.literal: The debate before the emperor was unresolved; he immediately bowed twice and asked to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: When debate before the emperor remained unresolved, he bowed twice and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「此小事，何必爾？」

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and said, "This is a small matter—why act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled: "This is a trifle—why take it so far?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「小事尚不伸，況大事乎！」

translations.literal: He replied, "If small matters cannot be upheld, what of great ones!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If I cannot prevail on a small matter, how can I prevail on great ones?"

sentences.zh: 帝為逐佐。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Zuo on his account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Zuo to satisfy him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，絳亦出知許州。

translations.literal: Before long Jiang also went out to govern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiang was also sent out to govern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，拜建雄軍節度使、知定州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng he was appointed military commissioner of Jianxiong Army and prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanfeng era (1078) he was appointed military commissioner of Jianxiong Army and prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為西太一宮使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as commissioner of the Western Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as commissioner of the Western Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 六年，知河南府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he governed Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he governed Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夏，大雨，伊、洛間民被溺者十五六。

translations.literal: In summer, great rains fell; between the Yi and Luo rivers five or six tenths of the people were drowned.
translations.idiomatic: That summer torrential rains drowned five or six tenths of the people between the Yi and Luo rivers.

sentences.zh: 絳發廩振恤，環城築堤，數月，水復至，民賴以免。

translations.literal: Jiang opened granaries for relief, built dikes around the city wall, and several months later when the water came again the people relied on this to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang opened granaries for relief and built dikes around the city; when floods returned months later, the people were saved by his works.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，更鎮江軍節度使、開府儀同三司，封康國公，為北京留守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, he was made military commissioner of Zhenjiang Army, Grand Preceptor with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Duke of Kang, and appointed defender of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended, he was made military commissioner of Zhenjiang Army, granted ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Duke of Kang, and appointed defender of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 河決小吳，都水議傍魏城鑿渠東趨金堤，役甚棘。

translations.literal: The river breached at Xiaowu; the Directorate of Waterways proposed cutting a channel east of Weicheng toward the Jin Embankment—the labor was extremely difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River breached at Xiaowu, the Directorate of Waterways proposed cutting a channel east of Weicheng toward the Jin Embankment—a laborious and difficult project.

sentences.zh: 絳言：「功必不成，徒耗費國力，而使魏人流徙，非計也。」

translations.literal: Jiang said, "The work will certainly not succeed; it will only waste state resources and cause the people of Wei to flee and disperse—this is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "The project cannot succeed; it will only waste state resources and displace the people of Wei—this is no sound plan."

sentences.zh: 三奏，訖罷之。

translations.literal: He memorialized three times, and in the end it was halted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized three times, and the project was finally abandoned.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年，請老，以司空、檢校太尉致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanyou he requested retirement and retired with the titles of Minister of Works and Acting Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yuanyou era (1087) he requested retirement and retired with the titles of minister of works and acting grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，諡曰「獻肅」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, with the posthumous title "Offering and Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand tutor and given the posthumous title Offering and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 絳臨事果敢，不為後慮。

translations.literal: Jiang was bold and decisive in handling affairs and did not look to consequences.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was bold and decisive in office and gave little thought to consequences.

sentences.zh: 好延接士大夫，數薦司馬光可用，終以黨王安石復得政，是以清議少之。

translations.literal: He liked to receive and entertain scholar-officials and repeatedly recommended that Sima Guang was usable; in the end because he sided with Wang Anshi in his return to power, pure critics held him somewhat in low regard.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed hosting scholar-officials and repeatedly recommended Sima Guang as capable; yet because he aligned with Wang Anshi's return to power, moral critics held him in lower esteem.

sentences.zh: 子 宗師

translations.literal: Son: Zongshi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zongshi

sentences.zh: 子宗師，字傳道，以父任歷州縣職。

translations.literal: His son Zongshi, courtesy name Chuandao, through his father's position served in successive prefectural and county posts.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongshi, whose courtesy name was Chuandao, entered service through his father's rank and held successive prefectural and county posts.

sentences.zh: 既登第，王安石薦為度支判官、提舉河北常平。

translations.literal: After passing the examination, Wang Anshi recommended him as judge of the Expenditure Bureau and intendant of Hebei Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the civil service examination, Wang Anshi recommended him as judge of the Expenditure Bureau and intendant of Hebei's Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 累官至集賢殿修撰、知河中府，卒。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to compiler in the Hall of Assembled Talents and prefect of Hezhong, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to compiler in the Hall of Assembled Talents and prefect of Hezhong, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 初，宗師在神宗朝，數賜對，常弗忍去親側，屢辭官不拜，世以孝與之。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Shenzong's reign Zongshi was repeatedly granted audiences; he often could not bear to leave his father's side and repeatedly declined offices without accepting them—the age praised him for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenzong's reign Zongshi was repeatedly granted imperial audiences; unable to leave his father's side, he repeatedly declined appointments, and contemporaries praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 韓維，字持國。

translations.literal: Han Wei, courtesy name Chiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei, whose courtesy name was Chiguo.

sentences.zh: 以進士奏名禮部，方億輔政，不肯試大廷，受蔭入官。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi and been listed at the Ministry of Rites, while Yi was assisting in government he refused to take the grand court examination and entered office by yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi and been listed at the Ministry of Rites, while his father Yi was in high office he declined the palace examination and entered service through hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 父沒後，閉門不仕。

translations.literal: After his father died he shut his doors and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he shut his doors and declined office.

sentences.zh: 宰相薦其好古嗜學，安於靜退，召試學士院，辭不就。

translations.literal: The chief minister recommended that he loved antiquity and delighted in learning, was content with quiet withdrawal, and he was summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy but declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister recommended him for his love of antiquity and learning and his contentment with quiet retirement; summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy, he declined.

sentences.zh: 富弼辟河東幕府，史館修撰歐陽修薦為檢討、知太常禮院。

translations.literal: Fu Bi recruited him to the Hedong staff; Ouyang Xiu, compiler of the Historiography Institute, recommended him as collator and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi recruited him to the Hedong staff; Ouyang Xiu of the Historiography Institute recommended him as collator and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 禮官議祫享東向位，維請虛室以待太祖。

translations.literal: Ritual officials debated the eastern-facing position in the joint zhao-xiang sacrifice; Wei asked to leave the chamber vacant to await Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When ritual officials debated the eastern-facing seat in the joint zhao-xiang sacrifice, Wei petitioned to leave the chamber vacant for Taizu.

sentences.zh: 溫成后立廟用樂，維以為不如禮，請一切裁去。

translations.literal: Empress Wencheng had a temple established with music; Wei regarded this as contrary to ritual and asked that it all be cut away.
translations.idiomatic: When a temple with music was established for Empress Wencheng, Wei deemed it uncanonical and petitioned to abolish the practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 議陳執中諡，以為張貴妃治喪皇儀殿、追冊位號，皆執中所建，宜曰「榮靈」，詔諡曰「恭」，維曰：「責難於君謂之恭，執中何以得此？」

translations.literal: In deliberating Chen Zhizhong's posthumous title, he held that the mourning for Noble Consort Zhang in the Hall of Imperial Rites, and the posthumous enfeoffment and title, were all established by Zhizhong and the title ought to be "Glorious Spirit"; the edict gave the title "Respectful"; Wei said, "To hold the ruler to account is called respectful—how can Zhizhong obtain this?"
translations.idiomatic: Debating Chen Zhizhong's posthumous title, he argued that the mourning for Noble Consort Zhang in the Hall of Imperial Rites and her posthumous enfeoffment were Zhizhong's doing and the title should be "Glorious Spirit"; when the edict gave "Respectful," Wei objected, "'Respectful' means holding the ruler to account—how does Zhizhong deserve that?"

sentences.zh: 議訖不行，乞罷禮院。

translations.literal: When deliberation ended without adoption, he asked to be dismissed from the ritual court.
translations.idiomatic: When his views were rejected, he asked to resign from the ritual court.

sentences.zh: 以秘閣校理通判涇州。

translations.literal: As collator of the Secret Archive he served as vice-prefect of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As collator of the Secret Archive he served as vice-prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 神宗封淮陽郡王、潁王，維皆為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Shenzong was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang and Prince of Ying, Wei served as recorder-general for both.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong was invested as Prince of Huaiyang and later as Prince of Ying, Han Wei served as recorder-general to each in turn.

sentences.zh: 王每事咨訪，維悉心以對，至拜起進趨之容，皆陳其節。

translations.literal: Whenever the prince consulted him on any matter, Wei answered with full care; even in the deportment of bowing, rising, advancing, and retreating, he explained every proper gesture.
translations.idiomatic: On every question the prince put to him, Wei answered with complete attentiveness—even the forms of bowing, rising, advancing, and withdrawing, he set out in full detail.

sentences.zh: 嘗與論天下事，語及功名。

translations.literal: Once when they discussed affairs of the realm, the talk turned to fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, as they discussed affairs under Heaven, their conversation turned to fame and merit.

sentences.zh: 維曰：「聖人功名，因事始見，不可有功名心。」

translations.literal: Wei said: "For the sage, fame and achievement appear only through affairs; one must not harbor a mind bent on fame and achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "For the sage, renown and achievement emerge only through the work at hand; one must never set one's heart on renown itself."

sentences.zh: 王拱手稱善。

translations.literal: The prince bowed with hands clasped and praised the remark.
translations.idiomatic: The prince bowed with clasped hands and commended the point.

sentences.zh: 聞維引疾請郡，上章留之。

translations.literal: When word came that Wei had cited illness to request a provincial post, the prince submitted a memorial asking that he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wei had pleaded illness to seek a provincial appointment, the prince submitted a memorial urging that he be kept at court.

sentences.zh: 時禁中遣使泛至諸臣家，為王擇妃。

translations.literal: At the time the inner palace sent envoys widely to the homes of various officials' families to choose a consort for the prince.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the inner palace dispatched envoys throughout the households of officials to select a bride for the prince.

sentences.zh: 維上疏曰：「王孝友聰明，動履法度，方向經學，以觀成德。

translations.literal: Wei submitted a memorial saying: "The prince is filial, friendly, and intelligent; his conduct conforms to propriety, and he is oriented toward classical learning—to observe the completion of his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wei submitted a memorial: "The prince is filial, amiable, and bright; his bearing accords with ritual, and he is devoted to the classics, that his virtue may reach its full maturity.

sentences.zh: 今卜族授室，宜歷選勲望之家，謹擇淑媛，考古納采、問名之義，以禮成之，不宜苟取華色而已。」

translations.literal: Now in choosing a clan and granting him a bride-chamber, one ought to select from families of merit and standing, carefully choose a virtuous lady, investigate the rites of betrothal and inquiry-of-name, and complete the marriage according to ritual—not grasp at mere beauty and glamour alone."
translations.idiomatic: In choosing a clan and bestowing a bride upon him, one should search among families of distinguished service, select a worthy lady with care, and follow the ancient meaning of the betrothal and name-inquiry rites, completing the union in proper form—not settle for dazzling looks alone."

sentences.zh: 左、右史闕，英宗訪除授例，執政曰：「用館閣久次及進士高第者。」

translations.literal: When the Left and Right Recorder posts were vacant, Yingzong inquired about the precedent for appointments; the chief ministers said: "Use those long in Hanlin service and top-ranked jinshi graduates."
translations.idiomatic: When the posts of Left and Right Recorder fell vacant, Yingzong asked what precedent governed appointments; the chief ministers replied, "Choose those long in Hanlin service and jinshi graduates of the highest rank."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「第擇人，不必專取高科。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Simply choose the person; there is no need to focus exclusively on top examination ranks."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Choose the man himself; there is no need to insist on the highest examination rank alone."

sentences.zh: 執政以維對，遂同修起居注、侍邇英講。

translations.literal: The chief ministers recommended Wei, and he was then made co-compiler of the Veritable Records and attended lectures at the Ying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers named Wei, and he was appointed co-compiler of the Veritable Records and attendant at lectures in the Ying Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝初免喪，簡默不言。

translations.literal: When the emperor had first completed mourning, he was terse and silent, speaking little.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had first ended his mourning period, he spoke little and kept his words spare.

sentences.zh: 維上疏曰：「邇英閣者，陛下燕閒之所也。

translations.literal: Wei submitted a memorial saying: "The Ying Hall is Your Majesty's place of leisurely repose.
translations.idiomatic: Wei submitted a memorial: "The Ying Hall is where Your Majesty withdraws for quiet study.

sentences.zh: 侍於側者，皆獻納論思之臣。

translations.literal: Those who attend at your side are all ministers who offer advice and deliberate on policy.
translations.idiomatic: Those who stand at your side are all ministers charged with remonstrance and deliberation.

sentences.zh: 陳於前者，非經則史。

translations.literal: What is set before you is nothing but the classics or histories.
translations.idiomatic: What is laid before you is nothing if not the classics or the histories.

sentences.zh: 可以博咨訪之義，窮仁義之道，究成敗之原。

translations.literal: Through this one may broadly consult and inquire, exhaust the Way of benevolence and righteousness, and investigate the origins of success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: There one may consult widely, pursue the full reach of benevolence and righteousness, and trace the roots of triumph and ruin.

sentences.zh: 今禮制終畢，臣下傾耳以聽玉音，陛下之言，此其時也。

translations.literal: Now that the mourning rites are complete, your ministers incline their ears awaiting the jade voice; Your Majesty's words—this is the time for them.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the mourning observances are finished, your ministers strain to hear your voice; this is the moment for Your Majesty to speak.

sentences.zh: 臣請執筆以俟。」

translations.literal: I request permission to take up my brush and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant asks leave to take up his brush and await your words."

sentences.zh: 進知制誥、知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Edict Commissioner and director of the Silver Terrace Office of Memorial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Edict Commissioner and put in charge of the Silver Terrace Office of Memorial Review.

sentences.zh: 御史呂誨等以濮議得罪，維諫曰：「誨等審議守職，不過欲陛下盡如先王之法而止爾。

translations.literal: The censor Lü Hui and others were punished over the Pu Yi controversy; Wei remonstrated: "Hui and the others carefully deliberated and upheld their duty—they merely wished Your Majesty to fully follow the laws of former kings, and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor Lü Hui and others were punished over the Pu Yi controversy, Wei remonstrated: "Hui and his colleagues weighed the matter carefully and held to their office—they sought only that Your Majesty follow the precedents of former kings to the full, and nothing beyond that.

sentences.zh: 請追還前詔，令百官詳議，以盡人情；

translations.literal: I ask that the previous edict be recalled and all officials be ordered to discuss it in detail, so that public sentiment may be fully heard;
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the earlier edict be withdrawn and all officials be summoned to deliberate at length, so that every shade of public feeling may be heard;

sentences.zh: 復誨等職任，以全政體。」
