translations.literal: and that Hui and the others be restored to their posts, so that the integrity of governance may be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: and that Hui and the others be restored to office, so that the dignity of government may remain intact."

sentences.zh: 既而責命不由門下，維又言：「罷黜御史，事關政體，而不使有司與聞，紀綱之失，無甚於此，乞解銀臺司。」

translations.literal: Soon afterward, when punitive orders bypassed the Chancellery, Wei spoke again: "Dismissing censors is a matter bearing on the integrity of governance, yet the responsible offices were not allowed to know—a breach of institutional order worse than this could hardly be found. I beg to resign from the Silver Terrace Office."
translations.idiomatic: Before long, when punitive orders issued without passing through the Chancellery, Wei spoke again: "To dismiss censors touches the very fabric of government, yet the responsible offices were given no word of it—there is no graver lapse of institutional order. I beg to be relieved of the Silver Terrace Office."

sentences.zh: 不從，遂闔門待罪。

translations.literal: His request was not granted, so he shut his gates and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When this was refused, he closed his gates and awaited judgment.

sentences.zh: 有詔舉臺官二人，維言：「呂誨、范純仁有已試之效，願復其職。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered the recommendation of two censorial officials; Wei said: "Lü Hui and Fan Chunren have proven records; I wish they may be restored to office."
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for the nomination of two censorial officials, Wei said, "Lü Hui and Fan Chunren have already proved their worth; I ask that they be returned to their posts."

sentences.zh: 翰林學士范鎮作批答不合旨，出補郡。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen drafted a reply that failed to accord with the imperial intent and was sent out to fill a prefectural post.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Fan Zhen drafted a written reply that missed the imperial intent and was sent out to serve as prefect of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 維言：「鎮所失只在文字，當涵容之。

translations.literal: Wei said: "Zhen's fault lay only in the wording; he ought to have been treated with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Zhen's error was only in the phrasing; he deserved forbearance.

sentences.zh: 前黜錢公輔，中外以為太重，連退二近臣，而眾莫知其所謂，自此誰敢盡忠者？」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qian Gongfu was dismissed, the court and the realm thought the punishment too heavy; now two close ministers are dismissed in succession while no one understands the reason—from this point, who would dare serve with wholehearted loyalty?"
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Gongfu was dismissed earlier, court and country alike judged the penalty too harsh; now two close ministers are removed one after another while no one knows why—from this day forward, who will dare speak with full loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 潁王為皇太子，兼右庶子。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ying became crown prince, Wei concurrently served as Right Vice Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ying was made crown prince, Wei was appointed concurrently as Right Vice Tutor.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，維進言：「百執事各有職位，當責任，若代之行事，最為失體。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Wei offered counsel: "Each of the hundred officials has his post and ought to bear responsibility; if others act in his place, that is the gravest lapse in proper form.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong took the throne, Wei offered counsel: "Every officer of state has his own charge and ought to answer for it; when one man acts in another's stead, propriety suffers most grievously.

sentences.zh: 天下大事不可猝為，人君設施，自有先後。」

translations.literal: Great affairs of the realm cannot be undertaken abruptly; the ruler's measures naturally have an order of priority."
translations.idiomatic: Great undertakings for the realm cannot be rushed; a ruler's policies must unfold in their proper sequence."

sentences.zh: 因釋滕文公問孟子居喪之禮，推後世禮文之變，以伸規諷，帝皆嘉納。

translations.literal: He then explained Duke Teng of Wen's questions to Mencius about mourning rites, extrapolating the changes in later ritual practice, to extend his remonstrance indirectly; the emperor praised and accepted it all.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to expound Duke Teng of Wen's questions to Mencius on mourning ritual and traced how later rites had changed, extending his indirect remonstrance; the emperor praised and accepted every point.

sentences.zh: 除龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王陶彈宰相韓琦為跋扈，罷為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Wang Tao impeached Chancellor Han Qi for arrogance and overbearing conduct; Tao was dismissed from his censorial post and made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Wang Tao impeached Chancellor Han Qi for overbearing conduct; Tao was removed from the censorate and appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 維言：「中丞之言是，宰相安得無罪？

translations.literal: Wei said: "If the supervising censor's words are correct, how can the chancellor be without fault?
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "If the supervising censor spoke truly, how can the chancellor escape blame?

sentences.zh: 若其非是，安得止罷臺職？

translations.literal: If they are not correct, how can only the censorial post be abolished?
translations.idiomatic: If he was wrong, how can only the censorial office be taken away?

sentences.zh: 今為學士，是遷也。」

translations.literal: Now made Hanlin Academician—that is a promotion."
translations.idiomatic: Yet now he is made Hanlin Academician—that is a promotion, not a demotion."

sentences.zh: 參知政事吳奎論陶事，出知青州。

translations.literal: Assistant Administrator Wu Kui spoke on Tao's case and was sent out as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Assistant Administrator Wu Kui spoke on Tao's case, he was sent out to govern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 維言進退大臣，不當如是。

translations.literal: Wei said that advancing and dismissing great ministers ought not to be handled in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said that the promotion and dismissal of great ministers ought not to be handled in this fashion.

sentences.zh: 詔遷奎官。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Kui's rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued raising Kui's rank.

sentences.zh: 維又言：「執政罷免，則為降黜；

translations.literal: Wei spoke again: "When a chief minister is dismissed, that counts as demotion;
translations.idiomatic: Wei spoke again: "When a chief minister is removed from office, that is demotion;

sentences.zh: 今復遷官，則為褒進。

translations.literal: now to promote his rank again is to honor and advance him.
translations.idiomatic: yet to raise his rank again is to honor and advance him.

sentences.zh: 二者理難並行，此與王陶罷中丞而加學士何以異？」

translations.literal: The two are logically hard to carry out together—how does this differ from Wang Tao's removal as supervising censor while being made Hanlin Academician?"
translations.idiomatic: The two cannot stand together in reason—how is this different from Wang Tao's removal as supervising censor paired with appointment as Hanlin Academician?"

sentences.zh: 章上，奎還就職。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Kui returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial reached the throne, Kui was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 維援前言求去，知汝州。

translations.literal: Citing his earlier words, Wei requested leave and was assigned to govern Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Invoking his earlier remonstrance, Wei asked to withdraw and was sent to govern Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 數月，召兼侍講、判太常寺。

translations.literal: After several months he was recalled to concurrently serve as Lecturer-in-Attendance and superintendent of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was recalled to serve concurrently as Lecturer-in-Attendance and superintendent of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 初，僖祖主已遷，及英宗祔廟，中書以為僖祖與稷、契等，不應毀其廟。

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Xianzu's spirit tablet had already been moved, and when Yingzong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Secretariat held that Xianzu stood on par with Hou Ji and Qi and that his temple ought not be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Emperor Xianzu's spirit tablet had been moved and Yingzong was to be enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Secretariat argued that Xianzu ranked with Hou Ji and Qi and that his temple should not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 維言：「太祖戡定大亂，子孫遵業，為宋太祖，無可議者。

translations.literal: Wei said: "Taizu quelled great disorder, and his descendants followed his enterprise as Song Taizu—on this there is nothing to dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Taizu brought the great chaos to an end, and his descendants carried on his work as founders of Song—on that there is no dispute.

sentences.zh: 僖祖雖為高祖，然仰跡功業，非有所因，若以所事稷、契事之，懼有未安，宜如故便。」

translations.literal: Although Xianzu was the high ancestor, when one looks up to trace his achievements, there is nothing he built upon; if we treat him as we treat Hou Ji and Qi, I fear unease would remain—better to keep things as they were."
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu, though counted as high ancestor, founded nothing upon which later glory could rest; to honor him as Hou Ji and Qi are honored would, I fear, sit ill—better to leave the arrangement as it stands."

sentences.zh: 王安石方主初議，持不行。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi was then upholding the initial proposal and would not allow Wei's view to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi was then championing the original proposal and refused to let Wei's recommendation take effect.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，遷翰林學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining he was transferred to Hanlin Academician and governor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xining era he was made Hanlin Academician and assigned to govern Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 明年，為御史中丞，以兄絳在樞府，力辭之。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Supervising Censor, but because his elder brother Jiang was in the Privy Council, he vigorously declined.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was named Supervising Censor, but with his elder brother Jiang serving in the Privy Council, he declined the post emphatically.

sentences.zh: 安石亦惡其言保甲事，復使為開封，始分置八廂決輕刑，轂下清肅。

translations.literal: Anshi also disliked his words on the baojia system and had him returned to Kaifeng; there he first established eight wards to adjudicate minor punishments, and the capital district grew orderly and sober.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi also resented his criticism of the baojia system and sent him back to Kaifeng, where he first divided the prefecture into eight wards to hear minor cases; the capital grew quiet and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 時吳充為三司使，帝曰：「維、充以文學進，及任煩劇，而皆稱職，可謂得人矣。」

translations.literal: At the time Wu Chong served as commissioner of the Three Departments; the emperor said: "Wei and Chong rose through literary accomplishment, and when given heavy duties both proved equal to them—this may truly be called finding the right men."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Chong was commissioner of the Three Departments; the emperor said, "Wei and Chong both entered service through literary talent, and when given arduous posts each proved himself—this is what it means to appoint the right men."

sentences.zh: 兼侍讀學士，充群牧使。

translations.literal: He was also made Lecturing Academician, and Chong was made commissioner of the Pasturage Office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was also made Lecturing Academician, and Chong was appointed commissioner of the Pasturage Office.

sentences.zh: 考試制舉人，孔文仲對策入等，以切直罷歸。

translations.literal: Examining decree-examination candidates, Kong Wenzhong passed with his policy response but was dismissed and sent home for excessive bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: While examining decree-examination candidates, he passed Kong Wenzhong on the strength of his policy response, yet Kong was dismissed and sent home for speaking too bluntly.

sentences.zh: 維言：「陛下毋謂文仲為一賤士，黜之何損。

translations.literal: Wei said: "Your Majesty must not think that because Wenzhong is a lowly scholar, dismissing him does no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Your Majesty must not suppose that because Wenzhong is a humble scholar, dismissing him costs nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣恐賢俊解體，忠良結舌，阿諛苟合者將窺隙而進，為禍不細。」

translations.literal: I fear the worthy and talented will lose heart, the loyal and upright will fall silent, and flatterers who seek easy agreement will watch for openings to advance—the harm will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: I fear men of talent will lose heart, the loyal will hold their tongues, and sycophants who trim to every wind will press forward at the first opening—the damage will be far from small."

sentences.zh: 安石益惡之。

translations.literal: Anshi came to dislike him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's hostility toward him only deepened.

sentences.zh: 樞密使文彥博求去，帝曰：「密院事劇，當除韓維佐卿。」

translations.literal: Privy Councilor Wen Yanbo requested to retire; the emperor said: "Privy Council affairs are heavy; Han Wei ought to be appointed to assist you."
translations.idiomatic: When Privy Councilor Wen Yanbo asked to step down, the emperor said, "The Privy Council's business is arduous; Han Wei should be appointed to assist you."

sentences.zh: 明日，維奏事殿中，以言不用，請郡。

translations.literal: The next day, as Wei presented business in the hall, because his words went unheeded he requested a provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when Wei addressed the throne in audience, finding his counsel ignored he asked to be sent to a commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿東宮舊人，當留以輔政。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are an old companion from the Eastern Palace; you should remain to assist in governance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are a veteran of the Eastern Palace; you should stay to help govern."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「使臣言得行，賢於富貴；

translations.literal: He replied: "If my words could be carried out, that would be worth more than rank and wealth;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "If my counsel were heeded, that would outweigh any honor or emolument;

sentences.zh: 若緣攀附舊恩以進，非臣之願也。」

translations.literal: to advance by clinging to old favor is not my wish."
translations.idiomatic: to rise by trading on old ties of favor is not what I seek."

sentences.zh: 遂出知襄州，改許州。

translations.literal: He was then sent out to govern Xiangzhou, then transferred to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Xiangzhou and later transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，召為學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year he was recalled as Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year he was recalled to serve as Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝曰：「天久不雨，朕日夜焦勞，奈何？」

translations.literal: Entering audience, the emperor said: "Heaven has long withheld rain; day and night I am consumed with worry—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: When he came before the throne in audience, the emperor said, "Rain has long been withheld; day and night I burn with anxiety—what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 維曰：「陛下憂閔旱災，損膳避殿，此乃舉行故事，恐不足以應天變。

translations.literal: Wei said: "Your Majesty grieves over the drought disaster, reduces your meals, and avoids the main hall—these are merely the customary observances, and I fear they are insufficient to respond to Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "Your Majesty mourns the drought, reduces your table, and withdraws from the main hall—but these are only the customary responses, and I fear they will not answer Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 當痛自責己，廣求直言。」

translations.literal: You ought to reproach yourself deeply and broadly seek forthright speech."
translations.idiomatic: You should examine your own conduct with severity and widely invite candid counsel."

sentences.zh: 退，又上疏曰：「近畿內諸縣，督索青苗錢甚急，往往鞭撻取足，至伐桑為薪以易錢貨，旱災之際，重罹此苦。

translations.literal: After withdrawing, he submitted another memorial saying: "In the counties near the capital, collection of green-sprout money is pressed with extreme urgency; people are often flogged to make up the quota, even felling mulberry trees for fuel to exchange for cash—in the midst of drought disaster they suffer this affliction anew.
translations.idiomatic: On retiring, he submitted another memorial: "In the counties around the capital, collection of green-sprout loans is pursued with brutal urgency; people are flogged to make quota, and some cut down mulberry trees for firewood to raise the cash—in the midst of drought they suffer this added torment.

sentences.zh: 若夫動甲兵，危士民，匱財用於荒夷之地，朝廷處之不疑，行之甚銳；

translations.literal: Yet when it comes to mobilizing armies, endangering soldiers and civilians, and draining the treasury on remote barbarian lands, the court handles it without hesitation and pursues it with great vigor;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when it is a matter of mobilizing armies, putting soldiers and civilians at risk, and pouring treasure into distant borderlands, the court acts without hesitation and pushes forward with fierce resolve;

sentences.zh: 至於蠲除租稅，寬裕逋負，以救愁苦之民，則遲遲而不肯發。

translations.literal: but when it comes to remitting rents and taxes, easing arrears, and saving the people in their distress, the court is slow and unwilling to act.
translations.idiomatic: but when it comes to remitting rents and taxes, easing unpaid levies, and relieving a people in misery, the court delays and holds back.

sentences.zh: 望陛下奮自英斷行之，過於養人，猶愈過於殺人也。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will rouse yourself to decisive action; to err in nurturing the people is still better than to err in destroying them."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to act with resolute judgment; to go too far in cherishing the people is still better than to go too far in destroying them."

sentences.zh: 上感悟，即命維草詔求直言。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to understanding and immediately ordered Wei to draft an edict seeking forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and at once ordered Wei to draft an edict calling for candid remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「意者聽納不得於理與？

translations.literal: Its gist read: "Might it be that in listening and accepting counsel I have fallen short of reason?
translations.idiomatic: Its gist ran: "Have I failed to heed reason in what I hear and accept?

sentences.zh: 獄訟非其情與？

translations.literal: Might lawsuits fail to reflect the truth?
translations.idiomatic: Have lawsuits failed to reflect the truth?

sentences.zh: 賦斂失其節與？

translations.literal: Might levies and collections have lost proper measure?
translations.idiomatic: Have levies and collections lost their proper measure?

sentences.zh: 忠言讜論郁於上聞，而阿諛壅蔽以成其私者眾與？」

translations.literal: Might loyal and forthright counsel be stifled before it reaches me, while many who flatter and obstruct to serve their private ends surround me?"
translations.idiomatic: Has loyal and forthright counsel been stifled before it reaches me, while flatterers who block the truth to serve themselves grow numerous?"

sentences.zh: 詔出，人情大悅。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, public sentiment was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict appeared, the people received it with widespread joy.

sentences.zh: 有旨體量市易、免行利病，權罷力田、保甲，是日乃雨。

translations.literal: An order was issued to assess the benefits and harms of market trading and exemption certificates, and to suspend temporarily the plowing-fostering and baojia systems; that very day rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: An order went out to weigh the benefits and harms of market trading and exemption certificates and to suspend temporarily the plowing-fostering and baojia systems; rain fell that same day.

sentences.zh: 王安石罷，會絳入相，加端明殿學士、知河陽，復知許州。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi was dismissed, and as Jiang entered the chancellery, Wei was made Academician of the Hall of Clarity and Brightness and assigned to Heyang, then again to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi left office and Wei's brother Jiang entered the chancellery, Wei was made Academician of the Hall of Clarity and Brightness and sent to Heyang, then again to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝幸舊邸，進資政殿學士。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited his former residence, Wei was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited his old princely residence, Wei was promoted to Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.

sentences.zh: 曾鞏當制，稱其純明亮直，帝令改命詞。

translations.literal: When Zeng Gong drafted the appointment text and praised him as pure, bright, and upright, the emperor ordered the commission wording changed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Gong drafted the appointment decree and praised him as pure, bright, and upright, the emperor ordered the wording revised.

sentences.zh: 維知帝意，請提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: Wei understood the emperor's intent and requested appointment as superintendent of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's mind, Wei asked to be made superintendent of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，赴臨闕庭。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, he hurried to the palace to mourn at the gate court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, he came at once to mourn at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后手詔勞問，維對曰：「人情貧則思富，苦則思樂，困則思息，鬱則思通。

translations.literal: Empress Xuanren sent a handwritten edict of inquiry and consolation; Wei replied: "In human nature, when poor one thinks of wealth, when suffering one thinks of ease, when exhausted one thinks of rest, when stifled one thinks of release.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xuanren sent a handwritten edict of inquiry and comfort; Wei answered, "Human nature is such that the poor long for wealth, the wretched for ease, the weary for rest, and the stifled for relief.

sentences.zh: 誠能常以利民為本，則民富；

translations.literal: If one can truly take benefiting the people as the foundation, the people will be rich;
translations.idiomatic: If you truly make benefiting the people your foundation, they will grow prosperous;

sentences.zh: 常以憂民為心，則民樂；

translations.literal: if one constantly keeps concern for the people at heart, the people will be content;
translations.idiomatic: if you keep the people's welfare always at heart, they will know contentment;

sentences.zh: 賦役非人力所堪者去之，則勞困息；

translations.literal: if corvée and levies beyond human endurance are removed, toil and hardship will cease;
translations.idiomatic: if levies and corvée duties beyond what human strength can bear are lifted, exhaustion will give way to rest;

sentences.zh: 法禁非人情所便者蠲之，則鬱塞通。

translations.literal: if laws and prohibitions inconvenient to human feeling are remitted, stifling obstruction will give way to openness.
translations.idiomatic: if laws and prohibitions that run against human nature are set aside, oppression will yield to relief.

sentences.zh: 推此而廣之，盡誠而行之，則子孫觀陛下之德，不待教而成矣。」

translations.literal: Extend this and broaden it; carry it out with full sincerity—then your descendants, observing Your Majesty's virtue, will attain completion without awaiting instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Extend this principle and act on it with full sincerity, and your descendants, seeing Your Majesty's virtue, will grow upright without needing to be taught."

sentences.zh: 未幾，起知陳州，未行，召兼侍讀，加大學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to govern Chenzhou; before he departed he was summoned to concurrently serve as Lecturer-in-Attendance and was given the grand academician title.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to govern Chenzhou, but before he could leave he was summoned to serve concurrently as Lecturer-in-Attendance and was raised to Grand Academician.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「先帝以夏國主秉常廢，故興問罪之師。

translations.literal: He once said: "The late emperor, because the ruler of Western Xia, Bingchang, had been deposed, therefore raised an army to call him to account.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The late emperor marched to punish Western Xia because its ruler Bingchang had been deposed.

sentences.zh: 今既復位，有蕃臣禮，宜還其故地。」

translations.literal: Now that he has been restored to the throne and observes the rites due a border vassal, we ought to return his former territory."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has been restored and again observes the rites of a border vassal, we ought to return the lands taken from him."

sentences.zh: 因陳兵不可不息者三，地不可不棄者五。

translations.literal: He then set forth three reasons why military action could not fail to cease and five territories that could not fail to be relinquished.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to set forth three reasons war must end and five territories that must be returned.

sentences.zh: 又言：「仁宗選建儲嗣，一時忠勲皆被寵祿；

translations.literal: He also said: "When Renzong chose and established the heir, the loyal and meritorious of that time all received honors and rewards;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When Renzong chose and established the heir apparent, every loyal servant of that hour was rewarded with honors and emoluments;

sentences.zh: 范鎮首開此議，賞獨不及，願褒顯其功。」

translations.literal: Fan Zhen was the first to open this proposal, yet reward alone did not reach him—I wish his achievement may be honored and displayed."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen was the first to raise this proposal, yet he alone received no reward; I ask that his service be publicly honored."

sentences.zh: 鎮於是復起用。

translations.literal: Fan was thereupon restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was thereupon brought back into service.

sentences.zh: 元祐更役法，命維詳定。

translations.literal: When the corvée law was revised in the Yuanyou era, Wei was ordered to compile and determine the details.
translations.idiomatic: When the corvée law was revised under Yuanyou, Wei was charged with drafting the detailed regulations.

sentences.zh: 時四方書疏多言其便，維謂司馬光曰：「小人議論，希意迎合，不可不察。」

translations.literal: At the time, memorials from all quarters largely spoke of its convenience. Wei said to Sima Guang: "The talk of petty men, seeking to read intent and curry favor — this cannot go unexamined."
translations.idiomatic: At the time, memorials from across the empire largely praised the measure's convenience. Han Wei told Sima Guang, "When petty officials speak, they often tailor their words to what they think you want to hear. Such talk cannot go unexamined."

sentences.zh: 成都轉運判官蔡曚附會定差，維惡而劾之。

translations.literal: The Chengdu transport-assistant magistrate Cai Meng had conformed to the fixed rank assignment; Wei detested this and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Meng, assistant magistrate of the Chengdu transport commission, had gone along with the fixed-rank assignment system. Han Wei despised this and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 執政欲廢王安石《新經義》，維以當與先儒之說並行，論者服其平。

translations.literal: The chief ministers wished to abolish Wang Anshi's New Classic Meanings; Wei held that they ought to run alongside the teachings of earlier Confucians, and commentators admired his even-handedness.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers wanted to abolish Wang Anshi's New Classic Meanings. Han Wei argued they should be allowed to coexist with the commentaries of earlier scholars, and critics on all sides respected his fairness.

sentences.zh: 拜門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 御史張舜民以言事罷，王岩叟救之，折簡密詢上官均。

translations.literal: The censor Zhang Shunmin was dismissed for speaking out on state affairs. Wang Yansou came to his defense and sent a private letter secretly asking Shang Guanjun about the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Shunmin was dismissed after speaking out on a policy matter. Wang Yansou intervened on his behalf and wrote a confidential letter to Shang Guanjun to inquire into the case.

sentences.zh: 語泄，詔岩叟分析。

translations.literal: Word of this leaked out, and an edict ordered Yansou to submit a written explanation.
translations.idiomatic: When word leaked, the emperor ordered Wang Yansou to submit a written explanation.

sentences.zh: 維曰：「臣下折簡聚談，更相督責，乃是相率為善，何害於理？

translations.literal: Wei said: "When ministers exchange letters and gather to discuss matters, urging one another on — this is leading one another toward the good. What harm is there in principle?
translations.idiomatic: Han Wei said, "When officials write one another, meet to discuss policy, and hold one another accountable, they are encouraging one another to do better. What principle does that violate?

sentences.zh: 若瑣瑣責善，懼於國事無益也。」

translations.literal: If one picks at such minor points of moral reproof, I fear it will do the state's affairs no good."
translations.idiomatic: If the court nitpicks every such exchange, I fear it will do the state no good at all."

sentences.zh: 維處東省逾年，有忌之者密為讒訴，詔分司南京。

translations.literal: Wei had served in the Eastern Secretariat for more than a year when someone who envied him secretly lodged slanderous accusations against him; an edict ordered him to serve in nominal capacity at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in the Eastern Secretariat, Han Wei was secretly denounced by a jealous rival. An edict sent him to serve in nominal office at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尚書右司王存抗聲簾前曰：「韓維得罪，莫知其端，臣竊為朝廷惜。」

translations.literal: Wang Cun, Right Section Chief in the Ministry of Revenue, spoke up loudly from before the screen: "Han Wei has been punished, yet no one knows the cause. Your servant privately grieves for the court."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cun, chief of the right section of the Ministry of Revenue, spoke up firmly from behind the curtain: "Han Wei has been punished, yet no one knows why. I cannot help feeling the court has lost something valuable."

sentences.zh: 乃還大學士、知鄧州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was restored to Grand Academician and made prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to grand academician and appointed prefect of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄絳為之請，改汝州。

translations.literal: His elder brother Jiang petitioned on his behalf, and his appointment was changed to Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Han Jiang petitioned on his behalf, and he was reassigned to Yuzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 久之，以太子少傅致仕，轉少師。

translations.literal: After a long while, he retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and was promoted to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he retired as junior tutor to the heir apparent and was promoted to junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，坐元祐黨，降左朝議大夫，再謫崇信軍節度副使，均州安置。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era, on account of the Yuanyou faction, he was demoted to Left Policy Advisor and later further banished as military vice commissioner of Chongxin Army, with residence enforced at Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng reign, he was punished as a member of the Yuanyou faction, demoted to Left Policy Advisor, and later banished again as vice military commissioner of Chongxin Army and placed under restricted residence at Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諸子乞納官爵，聽父里居。

translations.literal: His sons begged to surrender their ranks and titles so that their father might be allowed to live at home.
translations.idiomatic: His sons petitioned to surrender their own offices and titles in exchange for permission for their father to live at home.

sentences.zh: 哲宗覽奏惻然，許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong read the memorial, he was deeply moved and granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong was moved when he read the petition and granted it.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，以幸睿成宮，復左朝議大夫，是歲卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, on the occasion of the imperial visit to Ruicheng Palace, he was restored to Left Policy Advisor; he died that same year.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanfu, on the occasion of an imperial visit to Ruicheng Palace, he was restored to Left Policy Advisor. He died later that year.

sentences.zh: 年八十二。

translations.literal: He was eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-two years old.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，悉追復舊官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Huizong's reign, all his former offices were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Huizong's reign, all his former offices were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 韓縝，字玉汝。

translations.literal: Han Zhen, courtesy name Yuru.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhen, courtesy name Yuru.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，簽書南京判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and signed on as magistrate of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations and was appointed signing secretary and magistrate at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以水災求直言，縝上疏曰：「今國本未立，無以系天下心，此陰盛陽微之應。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong sought forthright counsel because of flood disasters, Zhen submitted a memorial saying: "The foundation of the state is not yet established, and there is nothing to bind the hearts of the empire. This is a sign of yin waxing and yang waning."
translations.idiomatic: After floods prompted Emperor Renzong to call for frank counsel, Han Zhen submitted a memorial: "The heir to the throne has not yet been firmly established, and the empire has nothing to fix its hopes upon. This is a sign of yin overpowering yang."

sentences.zh: 詞極剴切。

translations.literal: The language was extremely incisive.
translations.idiomatic: His language was painfully direct.

sentences.zh: 劉沆薦其才，命編修三班敕。

translations.literal: Liu Kang recommended his talent, and he was ordered to compile and revise the Three-Ranks Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kang recommended his ability, and he was assigned to compile and revise the edicts governing the Three-Ranks corps.

sentences.zh: 前此，武臣不執親喪。

translations.literal: Before this, military officers did not observe mourning for parents.
translations.idiomatic: Until then, military officers had not been required to observe mourning for their parents.

sentences.zh: 縝建言：「三年之服，古今通制；

translations.literal: Zhen offered counsel: "Three years of mourning is the universal practice of ancient and modern times;
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhen submitted a proposal: "Three years of mourning for a parent is the established practice in every age;

sentences.zh: 晉襄衰墨從戎，事出一時。」

translations.literal: Duke Xiang of Jin went to war wearing unhemmed hemp and ink-stained mourning cloth — that was a matter of the moment only."
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Xiang of Jin went to war in abbreviated mourning dress, that was an emergency exception, not a precedent to follow."

sentences.zh: 遂著令，自崇班以上聽持服。

translations.literal: Accordingly a regulation was issued: from the honored ranks upward, officers were permitted to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: A regulation was then issued allowing officers from the honored ranks upward to observe the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He became Attending Censor Within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 參知政事孫抃持祿充位；

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Sun Bian held salary and filled a seat;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Sun Bian was drawing salary while occupying a post in name only;

sentences.zh: 權陝西轉運副使薛向赴闕，樞密院輒畫旨除為真；

translations.literal: Acting transport vice commissioner of Shaanxi Xue Xiang came to court, and the Bureau of Military Affairs promptly drew up an edict making his appointment permanent;
translations.idiomatic: Acting Shaanxi transport vice commissioner Xue Xiang came to court, and the Bureau of Military Affairs immediately drafted an edict making his appointment permanent;

sentences.zh: 劉永年以外戚除防禦使；

translations.literal: Liu Yongnian was appointed defense commissioner on account of his connection by marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yongnian was appointed defense commissioner because he was an imperial in-law;

sentences.zh: 內侍史志聰私役皇城親從：縝皆極論之。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Shi Zhicong privately employed members of the Imperial City guard — Zhen vigorously argued against all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Shi Zhicong had privately put Imperial City guards to personal service — Han Zhen spoke forcefully against each of these abuses.

sentences.zh: 帝為罷抃，寢向與永年之命，而正志聰罪。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Bian on his account, shelved the appointments of Xue and Yongnian, and punished Zhicong according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed Sun Bian from office, set aside the appointments of Xue Xiang and Liu Yongnian, and punished Shi Zhicong by law.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史、度支判官，出為兩浙、淮南轉運使，移河北。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serving censor and revenue-section adjudicator, then sent out as transport commissioner of Liangzhe and Huainan, and later moved to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to serving censor and revenue-section adjudicator, then sent out as transport commissioner successively in Liangzhe, Huainan, and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 夏諒祚死，子秉常嗣，遣使求封冊。

translations.literal: Xia Liangzuo died; his son Bingchang succeeded him and sent envoys requesting investiture and a patent of rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzuo of Western Xia died, his son Bingchang succeeded him and sent envoys to request formal investiture.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方責夏人不修職貢，欲擇人詰其使。

translations.literal: The court was just then reproaching the Xia for failure to fulfill tribute duties and wished to choose someone to cross-examine their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The court was already reproaching the Xia for neglecting tribute obligations and wanted someone to cross-examine their envoys.

sentences.zh: 縝適陛辭，神宗命之往。

translations.literal: Zhen happened to be taking leave at court, and Emperor Shenzong ordered him to go.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhen happened to be at court taking leave of the throne, and Shenzong ordered him to go.

sentences.zh: 縝至驛問罪，使者引服，迨夜，奏上。

translations.literal: Zhen went to the post station and charged them with offenses; the envoys acknowledged guilt. By nightfall he had memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhen confronted the envoys at the post station, and they accepted blame. He memorialized the throne that same night.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，改使陝西。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and changed his assignment to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and reassigned him as envoy to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 入知審官西院、直舍人院。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as director of the Western Bureau for Reviewing Offices and keeper of the Drafting Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as director of the Western Bureau for Reviewing Offices and keeper of the Drafting Academy.

sentences.zh: 以兄絳執政，改集賢殿修撰、鹽鐵副使，以天章閣待制知秦州。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother Jiang held power in the government, he was reassigned as compiler at the Hall for Assembling Worthies and deputy salt and iron commissioner, then made Qinzhou prefect with the rank of Hanlin academician at the Tianzhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother Han Jiang was in power, he was moved to compiler at the Hall for Assembling Worthies and deputy commissioner of salt and iron, then appointed prefect of Qin Prefecture with the rank of Hanlin academician at the Tianzhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴客夜歸，指使傅勍被酒，誤隨入州宅，與侍妾遇，縝怒，令軍校以鐵裹杖箠殺之。

translations.literal: Once, after entertaining guests he returned home at night. The commander Fu Qin, drunk, mistakenly followed him into the prefectural residence and encountered a concubine. Zhen flew into a rage and ordered a military officer to beat him to death with an iron-shod club.
translations.idiomatic: Once, returning home at night after entertaining guests, he found that Commander Fu Qin, drunk, had mistakenly followed him into the prefectural residence and encountered a concubine. Han Zhen was enraged and ordered a military officer to beat him to death with an iron-shod club.

sentences.zh: 勍妻持血衣，撾登聞鼓以訴，坐落職，分司南京。

translations.literal: Qin's wife brought the bloodstained garment and struck the Court of Direct Petitions drum to lodge a complaint. Zhen lost his office and was assigned nominal duty at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qin's wife brought his bloodstained clothes and beat the drum at the Court of Direct Petitions to lodge a complaint. Han Zhen was stripped of his office and assigned nominal duty at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 秦人語曰：「寧逢乳虎，莫逢玉汝。」

translations.literal: The people of Qin had a saying: "Better to meet a nursing tigress than to meet Yuru."
translations.idiomatic: People in Qin had a saying: "Better to meet a tigress with cubs than to meet Yuru."

sentences.zh: 其暴酷如此。

translations.literal: Such was the violence and cruelty of his rule.
translations.idiomatic: That was how brutal he could be.

sentences.zh: 久之，還待制、知瀛州。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was restored to Hanlin academician and made prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was restored to Hanlin academician and appointed prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年，遼使蕭禧來議代北地界。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xining, the Liao envoy Xiao Xi came to negotiate the border in northern Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Xining era, the Liao envoy Xiao Xi came to negotiate the border in northern Dai.

sentences.zh: 召縝館客，遂報聘，令持圖牒致遼主，不克見而還。

translations.literal: Zhen was summoned to host the guest; then he was sent on a return mission bearing maps and documents to present to the Liao sovereign, but he could not obtain an audience and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhen was summoned to host the envoy, then sent on a return mission with maps and documents for the Liao ruler. He failed to obtain an audience and came back.

sentences.zh: 知開封府，禧再至，復館之。

translations.literal: As prefect of Kaifeng, when Xi came again, he once more served as host.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Kaifeng, he again served as host when Xiao Xi returned.

sentences.zh: 詔乘驛詣河東，與禧分畫，以分水嶺為界。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to travel by post relay to Hedong and, together with Xi, demarcate the border with the watershed as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to travel by post to Hedong, where he and Xiao Xi demarcated the border along the watershed line.

sentences.zh: 覆命，賜襲衣、金帶，為樞密都承旨，還龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: On reporting back, he was granted court dress and a gold belt, appointed chief courier of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and restored to Direct Academician of the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported back, he was granted court dress and a gold belt, appointed chief courier of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and restored to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，官制行，易太中大夫、同知樞密，進知院事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, when the new bureaucratic ranks took effect, he was redesignated Grand Master of Court and Deputy Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then promoted to Director of the Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the new rank system took effect in the fifth year of Yuanfeng, he was redesignated Grand Master of Court and deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then promoted to director of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，拜尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong acceded, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong took the throne, Han Zhen was appointed right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 首相蔡確與章惇謀誣東朝，及確為山陵使，縝暴其奸狀，由是東朝及外廷悉知之。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Cai Que conspired with Zhang Dun to slander the Eastern Court; when Que served as commissioner for the imperial tomb, Zhen publicly exposed his treacherous conduct, and from then on the Eastern Court and the outer court all knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Cai Que had conspired with Zhang Dun to slander the empress dowager. When Cai Que served as commissioner for Renzong's tomb, Han Zhen publicly exposed his treachery, and thereafter both the palace and the outer court knew what he had done.

sentences.zh: 確使還，欲以其屬高遵惠、張璡、韓宗文為美官。

translations.literal: When Que returned from his mission, he wished to reward his followers Gao Zunhui, Zhang Jin, and Han Zongwen with fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Que returned from his mission, he wanted to reward his followers Gao Zunhui, Zhang Jin, and Han Zongwen with lucrative posts.

sentences.zh: 宣仁后以訪縝，縝曰：「遵惠為太后從父；

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren asked Zhen about it. Zhen said: "Zunhui is the empress dowager's uncle by marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren asked Han Zhen's view. He replied, "Zunhui is the empress dowager's uncle by marriage;

sentences.zh: 璡者，中書郎璪之弟；

translations.literal: Jin is the younger brother of Secretariat attendant Zhang Sao;
translations.idiomatic: Jin is the younger brother of Secretariat attendant Zhang Sao;

sentences.zh: 宗文，臣侄也。

translations.literal: Zongwen is my own nephew.
translations.idiomatic: and Zongwen is my nephew.

sentences.zh: 今擢用非次，則是君臣各私其親，何以示天下？」

translations.literal: If they are now promoted out of turn, ruler and ministers will each be favoring their own kin — how is the empire to be shown an example?"
translations.idiomatic: If they are promoted out of turn now, ruler and ministers will each be advancing their own relatives. What example does that set for the empire?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon the appointments were halted.
translations.idiomatic: The appointments were dropped.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，御史中丞劉摯、諫官孫覺、蘇轍、王覿，論縝才鄙望輕，在先朝為奉使，割地六百里以遺契丹，邊人怨之切骨，不可使居相位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, Chief Censor Liu Zhi and remonstrating officials Sun Jue, Su Zhe, and Wang Di argued that Zhen's talent was mean and his reputation slight; that as envoy under the former emperor he had ceded six hundred li of territory to the Khitan; that men on the frontier hated him to the bone; and that he must not be allowed to hold the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou, Chief Censor Liu Zhi and remonstrating officials Sun Jue, Su Zhe, and Wang Di argued that Han Zhen was mediocre in ability and slight in reputation, that as an envoy under the previous reign he had ceded six hundred li of territory to the Khitan, that frontier people hated him bitterly, and that he must not be allowed to hold the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 章數十上，罷為觀文殿大學士、知潁昌府。

translations.literal: After dozens of memorials, he was removed and made Grand Academician at the Hall for Observing Culture and prefect of Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: After dozens of memorials, he was removed from the chief ministership and made grand academician at the Hall for Observing Culture and prefect of Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 移永興、河南，拜安武軍節度使、知太原府，易節奉寧軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yongxing and Henan, appointed military commissioner of Anwu Army and prefect of Taiyuan, then had his commission changed to Fengning Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred through Yongxing and Henan, appointed military commissioner of Anwu Army and prefect of Taiyuan, then had his commission changed to Fengning Army.

sentences.zh: 請老，為西太一宮使，以太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of age, was made commissioner of the Western Grand Unity Palace, and retired as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement, was made commissioner of the Western Grand Unity Palace, and retired with the rank of grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Shaosheng at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Shaosheng at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡曰「莊敏」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, with the posthumous epithet "Zhuangmin."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works, with the posthumous epithet Zhuangmin ("Dignified and Keen").

sentences.zh: 縝外事莊重，所至以嚴稱。

translations.literal: In outward affairs Zhen was grave and dignified; wherever he served he was known for severity.
translations.idiomatic: In public affairs Han Zhen was grave and dignified, and wherever he served he was known for strictness.

sentences.zh: 雖出入將相而寂無功烈，厚自奉養，世以比晉何曾云。

translations.literal: Although he rose to minister and general, he left behind no notable achievements; he indulged himself lavishly, and the age compared him to He Zeng of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to the highest ranks, he left no notable achievements behind, indulged himself lavishly, and contemporaries compared him to He Zeng of the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 子宗武。

translations.literal: His son was Zongwu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zongwu.

sentences.zh: 子 宗武

translations.literal: Son: Zongwu
translations.idiomatic: Son: Zongwu

sentences.zh: 宗武，第進士，韓宗彥鎮瀛州，辟為河間令。

translations.literal: Zongwu passed the jinshi examination. When Han Zongyan served as military commissioner at Yingzhou, he recruited him as magistrate of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwu passed the jinshi examinations. When Han Zongyan was military commissioner at Ying Prefecture, he recruited him as magistrate of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 值河溢，增堤護城，吏率兵五百伐材近郊，雖墓木亦不免，父老遮道泣，宗武入府白罷之。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River overflowed, dikes were raised to protect the city. Officials led five hundred soldiers to cut timber in the suburbs, sparing not even graveyard trees. The elders blocked the road weeping; Zongwu went to the prefectural office and reported this, and the practice was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River flooded, officials raised dikes to protect the city and led five hundred soldiers into the suburbs to cut timber, not sparing even graveyard trees. Elders blocked the road weeping. Zongwu went to the prefectural office and reported the abuse, and the order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，為秘書丞，因日食上疏言：「近世事有微漸而不可不察者五：大臣不畏公論，小臣趨利附下，一也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong acceded, he served as secretary director. On the occasion of a solar eclipse he submitted a memorial saying: "In recent affairs there are five gradual developments that cannot go unexamined: grand ministers do not fear public opinion, petty officials chase profit and attach themselves to their superiors — the first.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, Zongwu was secretary director. On the occasion of a solar eclipse he submitted a memorial: "Five gradual trends in recent affairs deserve close attention. First, senior officials no longer fear public opinion, while junior officials chase profit and attach themselves to powerful patrons.

sentences.zh: 人主怠於政事，威柄下移，怨讟歸上，二也。

translations.literal: The ruler neglects affairs of state, authority slips downward, and resentment is attributed to the throne — the second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the ruler neglects governance, authority slips to others, and public resentment is blamed on the throne.

sentences.zh: 左右無輔拂之士，守邊無禦侮之臣，三也。

translations.literal: At hand there are no advisors to assist and correct; on the frontier there are no ministers to repel insult — the third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the ruler lacks advisors who will speak plainly, and the frontier lacks ministers capable of repelling aggression.

sentences.zh: 開境土以速邊患，耗賦財以弊民力，四也。

translations.literal: Opening territory hastens frontier troubles; draining revenue exhausts the people's strength — the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, expanding territory only hastens frontier crises, while draining revenue exhausts the people's strength.

sentences.zh: 歲穀不登，倉庾空竭，民人流亡，盜賊數起，五也。

translations.literal: Year after year the harvest fails, granaries stand empty, the people flee, and bandits rise repeatedly — the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, harvests fail year after year, granaries run empty, people flee their homes, and banditry grows.

sentences.zh: 根治朋黨，追復私怨。

translations.literal: Rooting out factional cliques and settling old private grudges.
translations.idiomatic: Root out factional cliques and settle old private grudges.

sentences.zh: 正士黜廢，耆老殲亡，旋起大獄，害及善類。

translations.literal: Upright men are dismissed and cast aside; venerable elders are destroyed; great prosecutions are swiftly launched, and harm reaches the good as well.
translations.idiomatic: Upright men are dismissed, venerable elders destroyed, and major prosecutions launched that harm even the innocent.

sentences.zh: 文章號令，衰於前世。

translations.literal: Prose edicts and imperial commands have declined from those of earlier ages.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial writing and public orders have fallen below the standards of earlier reigns.

sentences.zh: 大河決溢，饑饉薦臻。

translations.literal: The great river breaks its banks and overflows; famine follows in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River breaks its banks repeatedly, and famine follows one upon another.

sentences.zh: 執政大臣，人懷異意，排去舊怨，以立新黨，徒為紛紛，無憂國忘家之慮。

translations.literal: Among the chief ministers in power, each harbors private designs; they drive out old enemies to establish new factions — nothing but turmoil, with no thought of caring for the state and forgetting self.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power each pursue private aims, purge old enemies to build new factions, and stir up endless turmoil without any thought of serving the state above personal interest.

sentences.zh: 誠願躬攬權綱，收還威柄，敷言奏功，考察名實，不以侍御之好、鐘鼓之娛為樂。

translations.literal: I sincerely wish that Your Majesty would personally grasp the reins of authority, recover sovereign power, heed good counsel and reward merit, examine names against reality, and not take delight in the pleasures of attendants and music.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly hope Your Majesty will take the reins of power back into your own hands, heed good counsel, reward real merit, judge men by their deeds rather than their titles, and not take your pleasure in attendants and amusements.

sentences.zh: 仁祖惻怛至誠，以收天下之心；

translations.literal: Emperor Ren was tender-hearted and utterly sincere in winning the hearts of the empire;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong's tender sincerity won the hearts of the empire;

sentences.zh: 神宗厲精不息，以舉天下之事；

translations.literal: Emperor Shen was vigorous and untiring in undertaking the affairs of the empire;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong's tireless energy drove the work of the state forward;

sentences.zh: 皆所宜法。」

translations.literal: both are worthy to be taken as models."
translations.idiomatic: both are examples worth emulating."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 哲宗將祔廟，中旨索省中書畫甚急。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong was about to be enshrined in the ancestral temple, an imperial order urgently demanded paintings from the Secretariat stores.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong was about to be enshrined in the ancestral temple, an urgent palace order demanded paintings from the Secretariat stores.

sentences.zh: 宗武言：「先帝祔廟，陛下哀慕方深，而丹青之玩，取索不已，播之於外，懼損聖德。

translations.literal: Zongwu said: "When the late emperor is enshrined in the temple, Your Majesty's grief and longing are still deep; yet the pursuit of paintings for amusement continues without end. If this spreads outside the palace, I fear it will damage Your Majesty's sacred virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwu wrote, "While the late emperor is being enshrined and Your Majesty's grief is still fresh, an endless search for paintings for amusement — if word of this spreads beyond the palace, I fear it will tarnish your reputation.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐祚，如日初升，當講劘典訓，開廣聖學，好玩易志，正古人所戒也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has just ascended the throne like the sun at its first rising; you should study the classics and ancient precepts, broaden your sacred learning — to indulge in amusements and lose resolve is precisely what the ancients warned against."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has just taken the throne, like the sun at first rising. You should study the classics, broaden your learning, and guard against distraction — indulgence at the start of a reign is precisely what the ancients warned against."

sentences.zh: 疏入，皇太后見之，怒曰：「是皆內侍數輩所為爾！」

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the empress dowager read it and said angrily: "This is all the doing of a few inner attendants!"
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the empress dowager read it and said angrily, "This is the work of a handful of inner attendants!"

sentences.zh: 欲盡加罰，帝委曲申救，乃已。

translations.literal: She wished to punish them all, but the emperor interceded tactfully on their behalf, and the matter ended there.
translations.idiomatic: She wanted to punish them all, but the emperor interceded on their behalf, and the matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 明日，太后對宰相獎嘆，令俟諫官員闕即用之。

translations.literal: The next day the empress dowager praised him before the chief ministers and ordered that when a remonstrating official's post fell vacant, he was to be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the empress dowager praised Zongwu before the chief ministers and ordered that he be appointed remonstrating official at the first vacancy.

sentences.zh: 尋除都官員外郎，改開封府推官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed outer department director of the Ministry of Justice and transferred to investigating magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed outer department director of the Ministry of Justice and transferred to investigating magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丐外，為淮南轉運判官。

translations.literal: He requested an outside post and became transport-assistant magistrate of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a provincial post and was appointed transport-assistant magistrate of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 前使者貸上供錢，禁庭遣使來索。

translations.literal: The previous commissioner had borrowed tribute funds; the palace sent envoys to collect repayment.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had borrowed funds meant for imperial tribute, and the palace sent envoys to collect repayment.

sentences.zh: 宗武奏具狀，詞極鯁切，坐貶秩，罷歸。

translations.literal: Zongwu memorialized with a full account; the language was extremely blunt. He was demoted in rank and dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwu submitted a full account in blunt language. He was demoted and sent home.

sentences.zh: 久之，蔡京欲以知潁州。

translations.literal: After a long while, Cai Jing wished to appoint him prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, Cai Jing wanted to appoint him prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝語秘書事，京不敢復言，遂致仕。

translations.literal: The emperor mentioned the Secretariat affair; Jing dared speak no further, and Zongwu retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor mentioned the earlier Secretariat affair, Cai Jing said nothing more, and Zongwu retired from office.

sentences.zh: 官累太中大夫，年八十二卒。

translations.literal: His offices cumulatively reached Grand Master of Palace Service; he died at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He rose cumulatively to grand master of palace service and died at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王稱曰：「昔袁安未嘗以贓罪鞫人，史氏以其仁心，足以覃乎後昆。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Wang Cheng said, "In former times Yuan An never interrogated anyone on charges of corruption; the historians, because of his humane heart, held that this was enough to extend blessings to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary states: Wang Cheng wrote, "In antiquity Yuan An never prosecuted anyone on corruption charges; historians judged that his humane heart alone sufficed to bless his descendants.

sentences.zh: 韓億不悅捃人小過，而君子知其後必大，皆盛德事也。

translations.literal: Han Yi disliked picking out people's minor faults, yet gentlemen knew his posterity would surely flourish—both are deeds of great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yi disliked nitpicking minor faults, yet gentlemen knew his line would flourish—both are acts of great virtue.

sentences.zh: 億有子位公府，而行各有適。

translations.literal: Yi had sons who reached the highest offices, and each man's conduct had its proper sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had sons who rose to the highest offices, each with his own distinctive character.

sentences.zh: 絳適於同，維適於正，縝適於嚴。

translations.literal: Jiang was suited to harmony, Wei to rectitude, and Zhen to severity.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang excelled in conciliation, Wei in uprightness, and Zhen in severity.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，維其賢哉！」

translations.literal: Alas, how worthy was Wei!"
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how worthy was Wei!"
